# MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE requirements

| ID | Requirement | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R001` | **Typed decision ladder with explicit resolution kinds (rollup).** Stages: 3 Policy and constraints to 7 Conclude, ops `AgentAssemble` and `Decide`. Every answer carries one `ResolutionKind`: constraint, entailment, optimization, statistical or abstention. The ladder applies policy and hard constraints first, then entailment, then the bounded exact solve. Fitted statistics only rank the remaining legal options or abstain. Children: `.1` the emitted kinds, `.2` the constraint and entailment paths, `.100` pre-surface safety bounds. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::AgentAssemble`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/assemble.rs::handle_agent_assemble` → `assemble_for` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::assemble` and `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::Decide`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs::handle_decide` → `decide_blocking`; both seal a record that carries `resolution_kind`. Shape: `ResolutionKind` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record.rs`; emitters `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/conclude.rs`, `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/seal.rs` and `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs`; the planned test drives one served case per kind. | Test: `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/resolution_tests.rs::every_resolution_kind_is_reachable_through_production_dispatch` (planned) (L3). It drives one served case per kind and asserts kind, `EvidenceClass` and premises. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R001.1` | **`ResolutionKind` is typed with all five variants; the production chokepoint emits Optimization, Statistical, and Abstention.** `ResolutionKind` (`crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record.rs`) defines Constraint, Entailment, Optimization, Statistical, and Abstention. The live assemble chokepoint (`crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/conclude.rs`, `seal.rs`) constructs `ResolutionKind::Optimization` and `ResolutionKind::Abstention`; `stat_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs`) constructs `ResolutionKind::Statistical`, `::Abstention` and, for an explicit task plan, `::Constraint`. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::AgentAssemble`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/assemble.rs::handle_agent_assemble` → `assemble_for` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::assemble` and `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::Decide`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs::handle_decide` → `decide_blocking`. Shape: the enum in `record.rs`; constructors at `conclude.rs`, `seal.rs` and `stat_decide.rs`. | Test: `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/tests/routing.rs::every_routing_item_answers_inside_its_acceptability_set`. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R001.2` | **Constraint and entailment resolution paths (rollup).** Stage: 7 Conclude, op `AgentAssemble`; `DecisionCommit` replays the result. Code: `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/conclude.rs::decide_one`, after `search` returns an answer on the plain path. The plain path has no template and no topology question. Templates and topology questions keep `Optimization`. A uniqueness re-solve proves that the hard model alone fixes selection S. Children: `.2.1` the constraint re-solve and record field, `.2.2` the entailment re-solve. `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs::seal` already emits `Constraint` for an explicit task plan; this row leaves that path unchanged. Depends: R001.101, R010.100. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::AgentAssemble`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/assemble.rs::handle_agent_assemble` → `assemble_for` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::assemble` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/conclude.rs::decide_one`. Shape: the uniqueness proof lives in the new `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/uniqueness.rs`, the field in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record.rs`, the replay in `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::replay_check`. | Test: `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/assemble_resolution_tests.rs::unique_selection_resolves_as_constraint_or_entailment` (planned) (L3). It asserts both kinds through served `AgentAssemble` and a byte-identical `DecisionCommit` replay. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R001.2.1` | **Constraint kind from a no-good re-solve.** Stage: 7 Conclude, op `AgentAssemble`. Code: new `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/uniqueness.rs::unique_selection`, called from `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/conclude.rs::decide_one` before `solved`. Rule: clone the solved `ModelSpec` and add one no-good row. The row is `sum(x_i, i in S) - sum(x_j, j not in S) <= len(S) - 1`. The objective becomes zero. The node budget is the same `effective_solver_budget` value. `Verdict::ProvenInfeasible` sets `ResolutionKind::Constraint`. Any other verdict keeps `Optimization`; an unresolved re-solve never guesses. Record: add `uniqueness: BoundedVec<UniquenessProof, 2>` to `DecisionRecord` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record.rs`. `UniquenessProof { scope: UniquenessScope, certificate: Certificate }` has scopes `AfterElimination` and `AllCandidates`. The field uses `serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BoundedVec::is_empty")`, so existing record bytes stay unchanged. `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::replay_check` re-derives the proofs and refuses a difference with `DecisionReplayMismatch`. Evidence: premise `unique_feasible_selection`, class `Proof`, provenance `Policy { policy_digest }`. Writes: none; `DecisionCommit` persists the record. Depends: R001.101, R010.100. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::AgentAssemble`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/assemble.rs::handle_agent_assemble` → `assemble_for` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::assemble` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/conclude.rs::decide_one` → `uniqueness::unique_selection` (new) → `crates/medulla-decision-policy/src/solve/search/mod.rs::solve`; replay: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::DecisionCommit`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/commit.rs::handle_decision_commit` → `commit` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::replay_check`. Shape: new `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/uniqueness.rs` (`unique_selection`) and new `UniquenessProof` and `UniquenessScope` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record.rs`; reuse the no-good row builder `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/search.rs::nogood` and `effective_solver_budget` from `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/request.rs`. | Test: `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/tests/uniqueness.rs::no_good_resolve_agrees_with_exhaustive_enumeration` (planned) (L2) compares the verdict to brute force. Verified by the root slice test `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/assemble_resolution_tests.rs::unique_selection_resolves_as_constraint_or_entailment` (planned). |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R001.2.2` | **Entailment kind from a re-solve over every candidate.** Stage: 7 Conclude, op `AgentAssemble`. Code: `uniqueness.rs::unique_selection` gains the `AllCandidates` scope, called after the R001.2.1 proof succeeds. Rule: rebuild the model over every candidate before `eliminate::screen` removes any, with the same no-good row. When `screened.eliminated` is empty, the R001.2.1 proof serves both scopes and no third solve runs. `ProvenInfeasible` in both scopes sets `ResolutionKind::Entailment`: `is_a` coverage alone fixed the answer. A feasible alternative in the `AllCandidates` scope keeps `Constraint`. The conclusion class stays the weakest class of the coverage derivation premises. Evidence: premise `unique_under_coverage_alone`, class `Proof`, provenance `NativeOntology { ontology_digest }`. Writes: none. Depends: R001.2.1. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::AgentAssemble`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/assemble.rs::handle_agent_assemble` → `assemble_for` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::assemble` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/conclude.rs::decide_one` → `uniqueness::unique_selection` (new). Shape: extend `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/uniqueness.rs` with the `AllCandidates` scope; reuse `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/eliminate.rs::screen` for the pre-elimination model and `UniquenessProof` from R001.2.1. | Test: `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/tests/uniqueness.rs::coverage_alone_fixes_the_answer_as_entailment` (planned) (L1). Verified by the root slice test `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/assemble_resolution_tests.rs::unique_selection_resolves_as_constraint_or_entailment` (planned). |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R002` | **Evidence class recorded on every decision record.** Each decision record stores an evidence_class: proof, observation or claim. The value comes from its weakest premise. Pack-provided capability annotations therefore appear as claims, not proof. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::AgentAssemble`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/assemble.rs::handle_agent_assemble` → `assemble_for` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::assemble` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/conclude.rs::solved` (the record `evidence_class` is `weakest` over the premises). Shape: `EvidenceClass` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record.rs`; `weakest` in `crates/medulla-decision-outcome-types/src/decision/derivation.rs`; pack-annotated capabilities enter as `PremiseClass::Claim` premises. | Test: `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/tests/planted.rs::a_pack_annotated_capability_is_shown_as_a_claim`. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R003` | **Derivation records for entailed answers.** An is_a derivation record backs an entailment-resolved answer. It names the source and premise class of each edge used. An invented or unsupported ontology edge bars the overall answer from claiming proof-level evidence. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::AgentAssemble`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/assemble.rs::handle_agent_assemble` → `assemble_for` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::assemble` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/conclude.rs::solved`; replay: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::DecisionCommit`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/commit.rs::handle_decision_commit` → `commit` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::replay_check`. Shape: derivation records and their verifier in `crates/medulla-decision-outcome-types/src/decision/derivation.rs`; reuse `weakest` for the chain class. | Test: `crates/medulla-decision-outcome-types/src/decision/derivation/tests.rs::a_tampered_chain_is_refused_at_the_step_that_lies`. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R004` | **Independently verifiable 0-1 integer solver certificate.** The solver in crates/medulla-decision-policy/src/solve produces a certificate for every solved assembly. It names feasibility, objective value, lower bound, optimality gap, solver version and input digest. A separate verifier recomputes and checks that certificate independently of the solve path. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::AgentAssemble`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/assemble.rs::handle_agent_assemble` → `assemble_for` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::assemble` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/search.rs::search` → `crates/medulla-decision-policy/src/solve/search/mod.rs::solve`; verify: `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::verify_solved` → `crates/medulla-decision-policy/src/solve/verify/mod.rs::verify`. Shape: `Certificate` in `crates/medulla-decision-policy/src/solve/certificate.rs`; the verifier shares no code with the search (`crates/medulla-decision-policy/src/solve/verify/`). | Test: `crates/medulla-decision-policy/tests/solve/exhaustive.rs::optimum_matches_exhaustive_search_on_random_small_models`; `crates/medulla-decision-policy/tests/solve/determinism.rs::repeated_solves_are_byte_identical`; `crates/medulla-decision-policy/tests/solve/determinism.rs::the_certificate_digest_matches_the_committed_golden_vector`. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R005` | **Conformal and risk-controlled statistical guarantees.** Statistical heads apply acceptability-set conformal prediction, selective risk control (Learn-then-Test) and adaptive conformal inference. Those bounds hold miscoverage under drift. When the guarantees cannot be met, a head abstains instead of returning an uncalibrated answer. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::DecisionFit`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/jobs.rs::handle_decision_fit` and `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::DecisionEval`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/jobs.rs::handle_decision_eval` → `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/fit_calibrate.rs` and `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/head_eval.rs`; served: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::Decide`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs::handle_decide` → `decide_blocking` → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_executor.rs::execute` → `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/ladder.rs::decide`. Shape: conformal sets and adaptive bound in `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/conformal/` (`sets.rs`, `adaptive.rs`); selective risk in `crates/medulla-numeric/src/risk/selective.rs::calibrate_selective_risk`; abstention via `AbstainReason::InsufficientConfidence` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record/outcome.rs`. | Test: `crates/medulla-numeric/tests/stat_kernels/risk.rs::selective_risk_controls_planted_risk_with_power`; `crates/medulla-numeric/tests/stat_kernels/conformal.rs::acceptability_sets_meet_the_acceptable_options_at_nominal_rate`; `crates/medulla-numeric/tests/stat_kernels/conformal.rs::adaptive_conformal_meets_its_long_run_bound_under_drift`. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R006` | **Off-policy evaluation gated on effective sample size.** Decision evaluation records exact propensities and computes off-policy estimates. It uses clipped or SWITCH importance sampling and doubly robust estimators. It reports effective sample size and refuses to promote a fitted head when that size falls below the configured minimum. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::DecisionEval`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/jobs.rs::handle_decision_eval` → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_evaluator.rs` → `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/evaluate.rs::evaluate` → `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/ope/`. Shape: estimators and support checks in `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/ope/estimators.rs` and `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/ope/logged.rs`; the ESS gate refuses promotion in `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/promotion.rs`. | Test: `crates/medulla-numeric/tests/stat_kernels/ope.rs::ess_gate_refuses_below_its_minimum`; `crates/medulla-numeric/tests/stat_kernels/ope.rs::support_checks_find_the_unsupported_action_and_its_mass`. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R007` | **Deterministic cross-target replay of committed decision records.** A committed decision record replays to byte-identical quantized fixed-point digests using a pinned software floating-point implementation. The same record verifies identically on every supported target platform. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::DecisionCommit`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/commit.rs::handle_decision_commit` → `commit` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::replay_check`; golden vectors in `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/tests/golden.rs`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R008` | **Why-chosen and why-not explanations for solved assemblies.** Every solved assembly can explain why it chose an option. For each visible excluded option, it can explain why not. It uses a bounded re-solve for that option rather than an unbounded search. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::AgentAssemble`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/assemble.rs::handle_agent_assemble` → `assemble_for` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::assemble` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble/why_not.rs::explain`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R009` | **Learned ranking stays monotone with respect to safety.** A fitted statistical head may only narrow the set of legal options or cause abstention. It can never widen the legal set. It can never authorize an option that policy and hard constraints have not already permitted. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::Decide`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs::handle_decide` → `decide_blocking` → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_executor.rs::execute` → `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/ladder.rs::decide` → `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/legal_option_filter.rs::derive_legal_options`. Shape: the legal set is fixed by `derive_legal_options` before any scorer runs; the scorer in `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/scorer/` receives only legal options; execution re-checks the set independently of the head. | Test: `crates/medulla-numeric/tests/decision/scorer.rs::an_eliminated_option_is_never_scored_and_moves_nothing`. |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R010.100.1` | **Refusal code type and family tables.** Add `RefusalCode` (a `&'static str` newtype) in the new `crates/medulla-types/src/refusal_code.rs`, the lowest crate that any family table needs, so a `medulla-types` module can declare a table without depending on `medulla-decision-types`; `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record/outcome.rs` re-exports it (`pub use medulla_types::refusal_code::RefusalCode`) and adds `RefusalOrigin` (closed: `Decide(QuestionKind)` or `Surface(RefusalSurface)`, where `RefusalSurface` is `DecisionLog`, `DecisionEval`, `Assemble`, `PolicyEvolution`, `DecisionCommit`), `AbstainReason::Family { family: QuestionKind, code: RefusalCode, detail: String }` for a `Decide` origin and `AbstainReason::Surface { surface: RefusalSurface, code: RefusalCode, detail: String }` for every other origin. `RefusalCode` serialises as its string; the decision crate decodes a string only into a registered code (`codes::resolve`). Each family module declares `pub const REFUSALS: &[RefusalCode]` (a table that also carries a meaning per code is `&[(RefusalCode, &str)]`); the tables of `medulla-types` and `medulla-source-types` modules (`belief_revision`, `claims`, `context_facts`, `meeting_transcript`, `transition_refused`, `lifecycle`) are collected by `codes::module_tables()` and the uniqueness test; a `Decide(kind)` origin selects the table of that `QuestionKind`, every other origin has one table named for it. Shared request codes live once in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/codes.rs`: `ACCESS_DENIED`, `PARAMETER_INVALID` and `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. Any family may return a shared code. A family table must not repeat a shared code or another family's code. `AbstainReason::code()` returns the stable code for every variant. Caller chain: `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::AgentAssemble`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/assemble.rs::handle_agent_assemble` → `assemble_for` → `crates/medulla-compute/src/assemble.rs::assemble` and `crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs::dispatch_decision_methods` (`Method::Decide`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs::handle_decide` → `decide_blocking` → any refusal reaches the wire through `AbstainReason::code()` (new) in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record/outcome.rs`. Shape: new `RefusalCode` newtype in `crates/medulla-types/src/refusal_code.rs`, its re-export and the `AbstainReason::Family` variant in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record/outcome.rs`; new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/codes.rs` for the shared codes; reuse `DecisionErrorCode` (`crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/errors.rs`) and `StatisticalErrorCode` (`crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/errors.rs`) as the existing request-code sources. | Test: `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record/outcome.rs::tests::codes_are_unique_and_stable` (planned) collects every table and every fixed variant. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R010.100.2` | **Fold existing per-feature refusal enums.** `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/record/outcome.rs` declares `trait DecisionRefusal { fn code(&self) -> RefusalCode; fn detail(&self) -> String; }` and `AbstainReason::from_refusal(origin: RefusalOrigin, refusal: &impl DecisionRefusal) -> AbstainReason`. Each existing abstain or refusal enum implements `DecisionRefusal` where it is declared (the trait is in the lowest decision crate, so no crate depends upward). It keeps its typed variants and maps each one to one registered code, so no refusal reaches the wire as a catch-all. The caller that raises the refusal knows the origin and passes it: a refusal raised on the `Decide` path passes `RefusalOrigin::Decide(kind)` with the request's `QuestionKind`; `PolicyRefusal` passes `PolicyEvolution`, the assembly refusals pass `Assemble`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R032.2.1` | **Isotonic calibration method for binary heads.** Stage: 10 Learn, op `DecisionFit`. Code: `CalibrationMethod` (`crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/outcome.rs`) already has `Isotonic`. `DecisionFitRequest` (`crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/jobs.rs`) gains `calibration_method: Option<CalibrationMethod>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, so existing requests keep their digest); `None` keeps the ladder's current choice, and only `Conformal`, `Temperature` and `Isotonic` are accepted, any other value refusing with `CALIBRATION_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED`. `HeadCalibration` (`crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/head.rs`) gains `isotonic: Option<IsotonicTable>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`), where `IsotonicTable { blocks: BoundedVec<IsotonicBlock, 1024> }` and `IsotonicBlock { lower: QuantisedValue, upper: QuantisedValue, value: QuantisedValue }` copy the monotone blocks of `IsotonicFit` in increasing order. Serving: `calibration_statement` (`crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/head_eval.rs`) reports `Isotonic` when `isotonic` is `Some`, and `Decide` maps the positive-class score to the `value` of the block whose `[lower, upper]` holds it (the nearest block outside the range), so the served probability equals `IsotonicFit::predict`. `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/fit_calibrate.rs::calibrate` calls `crates/medulla-numeric/src/calibration/isotonic.rs::fit_isotonic_weighted` when the fit request names `Isotonic`. Rule: isotonic applies to two-class heads only; a multi-class request refuses with `ISOTONIC_REQUIRES_BINARY`. The split-conformal threshold then runs over the isotonic probabilities. Writes: the fit job writes the draft head. Depends: R010.100. Shape: the request field and `IsotonicTable` above (`DecisionFitRequest::new` gains the argument); branch in `calibrate`; reuse `fit_isotonic_weighted`; branch in `calibration_statement`; refusals `ISOTONIC_REQUIRES_BINARY` and `CALIBRATION_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED` are registered `StatisticalErrorCode` variants (the closed refusal vocabulary of `Decide`, `DecisionFit` and `DecisionEval`). The positive class is the first option of a two-option item; the isotonic fit reads scores on the Q32 grid, so the served probability is exactly `IsotonicFit::predict` over the stored blocks, and `Decide` over a head with an isotonic table refuses any candidate set that is not two options with `ISOTONIC_REQUIRES_BINARY`. | Test: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/fit_calibrate.rs::tests::isotonic_calibration_is_monotone_and_reproducible` (planned) (L1). The default epsilon is 0.02, range [0, 0.2], on the probability scale; the knob is a decision-policy knob in `knob_families/route.rs`. Refusals: a tie-set option without a ledger entry abstains with `AbstainReason::UnknownFact { field: "l5.observed_cost" }` (R039.1). Scope: only an advisory score list is tie-broken; a calibrated act keeps its licensed option and a rule-stage answer keeps its rule. An option with a tie set of one needs no cost. Replay of an abstained record reads the costs sealed in its premises (`route.rs::replay_cost_tie`). Writes: none. Depends: R001.101, R801, R179. Payloads are serde structs in new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/memory_events.rs`: `DerivationCompleted { scope_id, session_id, subject, observer, claims_written, last_turn_id }`, `ClaimChanged { claim_id, from, to, subject, observer }` and `CardUpdated { subject, observer, card_digest }`, with one `topic()` table. Each event reaches the graph outbox as one `MemoryEvent` node (`MemoryEvent::node_operation`) in the `BatchUpdate` that writes the change it announces; the batch compiler (`memory_event_intents` in `crates/medulla-server-api/src/batch_compile/compile/finish_helpers.rs`) turns each such node into one `MutationOutboxIntent { topic, key, payload, headers }` of the same batch, so the outbox row is atomic with the write. The key is the subject id. Headers carry `tenant` and `event_kind`. Emitters: `CompleteDerivation` (R651.12) writes the first with its checkpoint; the `refresh_card` write (R655.3) writes the third with the card node. The claims stay in the statechart store, which a graph batch cannot join, so the second event follows the claim's own transaction: the `Claims` handler (R652.3) commits the transition and one outbox record of the same topic in the claim store's own transaction (`StatechartStore::send_event_with_outbox`), and the memory event publisher (`crates/medulla-h-jobs/src/memory_event_publisher.rs`) is the one reader of those rows: it leases each under the consumer `memory-event-publisher`, writes the `MemoryEvent` node to the graph named by the row's `graph` header as an engine-internal batch whose id derives from the row (`MemoryEvent::row_node_id`), and only then acknowledges the row, so a republish after a crash replays the same batch. The router calls the publisher after every claim commit, and the leader tick calls it on every pass, so a row whose publish never happened is published by the next tick. The event is never sent before the claim commits. Only a claim that has a perspective emits; the claim store's row stays if the graph write fails, and the failure is logged as `MEMORY_EVENT_PUBLISH_FAILED`. Rule: generated means a header line containing `@generated` or `DO NOT EDIT`. Lockfile means a path ending in `Cargo.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `poetry.lock` or `uv.lock`. Vendored means a path segment `vendor`, `node_modules` or `third_party`. Minified means a line of at least `knob embedding.minified_line_chars` characters (default 1000, [200, 100000]). Excluded classes skip embedding through `ContentClass::admits`. A span whose SHA-256 digest matches an already embedded span in `web::prior_enrichments` skips as `SkippedExact`: no embedding call is made and the prior vector is reused. The four `embedding.*` thresholds are `Tunable` knobs registered in the knob registry and read through `DecisionPolicy::knob`. Evidence: `EnrichDocumentReceipt` gains `admissions`, one `UnitAdmission { ordinal, class, outcome }` per span with `outcome` the closed enum `AdmissionOutcome`, and `embedded_units`, the count of texts passed to the embedder. R113.2.1 refuses a capacity-backed topology decision because no path publishes the record, the lease and the evidence together. This row is that path. Owners: the Agent Library redb (`crates/medulla-persistence-records/src/agent_library.rs`, file `agent_library.redb`) holds the decision record (`commit_decision_record`, `crates/medulla-persistence-records/src/decision_record.rs:255`) and the graph evidence (`publish_graph`, `crates/medulla-persistence-records/src/agent_graph/write.rs:36`, whose `synthesis_evidence` field is the evidence reference); the capacity ledger holds the lease in `capacity_leases` of a graph shard through `Method::AcquireCapacity` (`crates/medulla-resource-store/src/redb_store/capacity_lease.rs`, `apply` at line 317, `commit` at line 166). New `crates/medulla-persistence-records/src/decision_record/shared_commit.rs` (new, declared in `decision_record.rs`) defines `AgentLibraryStore::commit_topology_decision(context, record, expected_catalog_digest, evidence: AgentGraphPublishRequest, coordinator_txn: &str) -> Result<TopologyCommitParts, String>` (`coordinator_txn` is the coordinator transaction id: an admission fence it holds itself does not block its write, any other holder refuses `ADMISSION_WRITE_BLOCKED`). It writes the decision-record component revision and the evidence graph revision in ONE `mutations.open_write` transaction of the Agent Library owner, so those two are never visible apart, and it is a no-op replay when the record is already stored. The capacity lease is the second participant. `DecisionCommit` already runs the owner-only certificate coordinator of R036.105.2 (no multi-raft exists for it on a single node), so the lease joins that sequence: `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/commit/capacity.rs` (`LeaseHold::acquire`) sends ONE `AcquireCapacity` carrying every positive `plan.lease.per_cell` demand through `PersistenceBackend::commit_capacity_lease` on the ledger graph the request names (the ledger grants all cells or none), idempotent on the coordinator transaction id so a resumed commit replays the same leases. It runs after the owners reserve and before the vote, as the lease participant's checked prepare. The wire request gains `topology: Option<TopologyCommitEvidence { capacity_graph, evidence: AgentGraphPublishRequest }>` (required for a capacity-backed plan, refused with `DERIVATION_REJECTED` otherwise; the capacity graph must be one the caller may write, and the evidence context is bound to the verified request); the result gains `topology: Option<TopologyCommitOutcome { evidence_graph_id, evidence_revision, premises }>` with one `lease:<id>` premise per lease. The lease lifetime is the registry knob `topology.lease_ttl_ms`. The Agent Library write runs only after the durable COMMIT decision of R036.105.2 and is finished by recovery from that decision when the process stops in between; an ABORT releases the leases with `ReleaseCapacity` under the same transaction key. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R113.3.2` | **Durable denial allowance consumption.** Stage: 9 Commit, served by `DecisionCommit`. A denied commit writes the `Issued` allowance row in the same transaction as its ABORT: the allowance owner is a participant of the certificate coordinator transaction. The denial stages the allowance on its Agent Library reservation (`AgentLibraryStore::stage_abort_allowance`) before the coordinator decides; the durable ABORT resolves the reservation, and `resolve_admission` applies the staged allowance in the owner transaction that releases it. A request replayed after a crash between the durable ABORT and the owners' resolution answers `CERTIFICATE_DECIDED_ABORT` and applies the same resolution, so the abort and the allowance are never separated; a COMMIT discards the staged row. Issuing is idempotent and a repeated denial after consumption grants nothing, because the tombstone is never reset. Depends: R113.2.3, R113.3.1.1, R010.100.1. Caller chain: `Method::DecisionCommit` -> `handle_decision_commit` (crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/commit.rs:22) -> `consume_denial_allowance` (new, crates/medulla-persistence-records/src/decision_record.rs). Code: `plan_over_skills(query, &[SkillDocument], &SkillPlanKnobs) -> Result<TaskPlanProposal, String>` in the stats file. `SkillPlanKnobs::from_policy` (types file) reads the three knobs from the pinned decision policy (`knob_families/task_plan.rs`, DECISIONS DE-R059.1-KNOBS). The output task is one of the subtasks. Rule: score each subtask against the visible skill texts with the candidate-local `bm25::scores` (`crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/bm25.rs`). Relevance is `s / (s + knob skill_plan.bm25_saturation)` (default 2.0, [0.1, 20], BM25 units), quantised once to Q32. Pick the best skill per subtask when relevance (an exact integer comparison on Q32) is at least `knob skill_plan.relevance_floor` (default 0.2, [0, 1], fraction). Ties go to the lowest skill id. Merge only when the joined prompt stays within `knob skill_plan.split_prompt_bytes` (default 4096, [256, 16384], bytes). The merged task keeps the lowest id. Split a subtask whose prompt exceeds that knob into a chain of parts `<id>.1`, `<id>.2`, cut at line boundaries (a single line longer than the knob is cut at the last character boundary that fits). The last part keeps the original dependants, and an output task that was split is renamed to its last part. The skills are read in the family's `conclude` path through `AgentLibraryStore` for the request's tenant and filtered to `Published`. Order is the canonical order `plan_explicit_tasks` derives. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R137.8` | **Package lowering and exact selection kernel.** Stage: 5 Exact solve. Code: new file `crates/medulla-decision-policy/src/solve/context_package.rs` in `medulla-decision-policy` (feature `solve`), reusing `Model`, `ModelSpec` and `solve` from `crates/medulla-decision-policy/src/solve/`. Fn `lower(request: &ContextPackageRequest) -> Result<(ModelSpec, u64), PackageRefusal>` returns the model and the effective capacity. `select(request)` runs `solve` under the request node budget and `verify`, and returns the chosen package only for a verified optimum with zero gap; `PackageRefusal{code, detail}` carries a closed `ContextPackageErrorCode`, including `CONTEXT_PACKAGE_MISSING_FACT`. One 0-1 variable stands for each candidate. Each evidence unit gets a `Linear` constraint `sum <= 1`. One `Linear` knapsack constraint limits total `token_weight` to the capacity. Capacity is the minimum of: `window - reserved_output` (zero when negative), the caller ceiling, `floor(money_ceiling / price)` and `floor(latency_ceiling_ms * tokens_per_second / 1000)`. A ceiling joins the minimum only when supplied. A known zero price drops the money term. A known zero throughput gives capacity zero. A ceiling whose rate is missing refuses `CONTEXT_PACKAGE_MISSING_FACT`. All arithmetic is checked. Objective level one minimizes the negated net value, where net is `value_micro - value_floor_micro_per_token * token_weight`. Level two minimizes total tokens. Candidate order is the order of `candidate_id`, which breaks remaining ties. `medulla_plan::context_bundle::compile` is a second in-process caller of `lower`, `solve` and `verify`. Writes: none; `Decide` is evaluate-only (AD-4). The evaluation preserves the independent-outcome join and hard-negative store of R100. Overstory and Meristem producers consume the receipt. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R100.101.1` | **Grounded topic coverage.** Stage: 10 Learn, served by `DecisionEval` through the new `DecisionEvalOp::GroundedAnswerSubmit` (wired in R100.101.3). Code: types in the new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/grounded_eval.rs`; kernel `topic_coverage` in the new `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/grounded_eval.rs`. `GroundedScope` is `SingleDocument`, `LocalMultiDocument` or `GlobalCorpus`. `ExpectedTopicSet` holds a query id and a non-empty list of unique topic ids. `TopicSupport` binds one topic id to its answer claim ids. Each claim binds to citation ids with support votes. The votes are `supporting` and `total`, both counts of valid independent votes. Rule: a topic is covered when one mapped claim cites a source with support fraction `supporting / total` of at least `knob grounded.min_topic_support`. Knobs: `knob grounded.min_topic_support` default 0.5, range [0.5, 1], unit ratio. `knob grounded.min_valid_votes` default 3, range [1, 25], unit votes. A citation with fewer than `grounded.min_valid_votes` votes refuses scoring. The result lists `expected_topic_ids` and `covered_topic_ids` per query. Per scope, coverage is the summed covered count over the summed expected count of the pinned query set. It is never an average of per-query ratios. Refusals, in the new `grounded_eval` family table: `GROUNDED_QUERY_SET_EMPTY`, `GROUNDED_TOPIC_SET_EMPTY`, `GROUNDED_VOTES_TOO_FEW`, `GROUNDED_TOPIC_DUPLICATE`. Writes: none. Caller chain: wire `Method::DecisionEval` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:126`) → `handle_decision_eval` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/jobs.rs:30`) → `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/grounded_eval.rs` → `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/grounded_eval.rs`. Shape: files `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/grounded_eval.rs` (new); `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/grounded_eval.rs` (new); reuse `handle_decision_eval` in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/jobs.rs:30`. Depends: R010.100.1, R179.1. | Test: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/grounded_eval.rs::tests::coverage_sums_numerators_before_dividing` (L1) uses two queries with different topic counts and asserts the pooled ratio and each refusal. Verified by the root slice test `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/grounded_eval_tests.rs::grounded_evaluation_is_sealed_with_scorer_isolation` (L3). |
Depends: MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R010.100.1, MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R179.1
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R100.101.2` | **Soft-label unsupported-claim Brier score.** Stage: 10 Learn, served by `DecisionEval` through `GroundedAnswerSubmit`. Code: types `GroundedClaimPrediction` and `ClaimVotes` in `grounded_eval.rs` (types crate); kernel `weighted_brier` in the `grounded_eval.rs` kernel file. `GroundedClaimPrediction` holds `claim_id`, `answer_digest`, `input_digest`, `scorer_id`, `scorer_revision`, `scorer_artifact_digest` and `p_ppm` (predicted unsupported probability in [0, 1000000]). `ClaimVotes` holds `claim_id`, a list of unique annotator refs with votes, `unsupported_votes` and `supported_votes`. The valid vote count `v` is their sum. Rule: the target `q` is `unsupported_votes / v`, rounded half to even to parts per million. For the required claim set `C`, the numerator is the sum of `v * (p - q)^2`. It uses parts per million squared in 128-bit integers. The denominator is the sum of `v`. The score is `numerator / (denominator * 10^12)`, rounded half to even to `knob grounded.score_digits` decimal digits. Knob: `knob grounded.score_digits` default 6, range [2, 9], unit decimal digits. The rounding mode is `Fixed`. Each claim in `C` needs exactly one prediction and at least one valid vote. Labelled votes never replace a detector prediction. Refusals: `GROUNDED_CLAIM_SET_EMPTY`, `GROUNDED_PREDICTION_MISSING`, `GROUNDED_PREDICTION_EXTRA`, `GROUNDED_ANNOTATOR_DUPLICATE`, `GROUNDED_VOTES_ZERO`, `GROUNDED_PROBABILITY_OUT_OF_RANGE`. Writes: none. Caller chain: wire `Method::DecisionEval` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:126`) → `handle_decision_eval` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/jobs.rs:30`) → the family module named in Shape. Shape: files the files named in Code, plus the knob table `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/knob_families/grounded.rs` (`grounded.score_digits`, read through `DecisionPolicy::knob`); the kernel is `weighted_brier(claims, predictions, votes, digits)` and the target is `target_ppm`; reuse `handle_decision_eval` in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/jobs.rs:30`. Depends: R100.101.1. | Test: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/grounded_eval.rs::tests::brier_changes_by_the_formula_when_only_p_varies` (L1) holds labels fixed, varies only `p_ppm` and asserts the exact numerator, denominator and score. It also asserts each refusal. Verified by the root slice test `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/grounded_eval_tests.rs::grounded_evaluation_is_sealed_with_scorer_isolation` (L3). |
Depends: MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R100.101.1
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R100.101.3` | **Grounded evaluation wiring, scorer isolation and evidence.** Stage: 10 Learn, served by `DecisionEval`. Code: add `DecisionEvalOp::GroundedAnswerSubmit { request: Box<GroundedAnswerRequest> }` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/jobs.rs`. Add the arm in `serve_eval` of `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_jobs.rs`, delegating to the new `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_grounded_eval.rs::submit`. Add `DecisionJobOutput::GroundedEval { receipt: Box<GroundedEvalReceipt> }`. `GroundedAnswerRequest` binds corpus, query, answer, claim, citation and label-set revisions as `PinnedSet`s (id, revision, digest), carries the content those pins name (expected topics, citation support, required claim ids, predictions, votes) and a `GroundedScorerRecord`, and names the policy by `DecisionPolicyRef`. The handler recomputes the digest of every content-bound set (all but the corpus) and stores `(set id, revision) -> digest` under a `grounded-pin:` key with the first accepted evaluation. `GROUNDED_DIGEST_MISMATCH` means a bound digest is not the digest of its content or of the stored revision. `GROUNDED_REVISION_STALE` means a newer revision of the set is already stored. The knobs `grounded.min_topic_support` and `grounded.min_valid_votes` resolve through the policy. Digests are SHA-256 with 64 lowercase hex characters. It also binds the scope, the evaluator revision and the policy revision. `GroundedEvalReceipt` holds per-scope topic coverage with numerator, denominator, covered ids and expected ids. It holds the Brier numerator, denominator and score, and every bound digest. Rule: the scorer record lists the digests of every input it read. The handler refuses when the label-set digest appears in that list. The handler refuses any request whose bound digest differs from the stored digest of that revision. `Method::UnifiedQuery` supplies the retrieved evidence and `DecisionEval` seals the receipt. Refusals: `GROUNDED_SCORER_SAW_LABELS`, `GROUNDED_REVISION_STALE`, `GROUNDED_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`, plus the codes of R100.101.1 and R100.101.2. Evidence premises: `grounded:scope=<scope>`, `grounded:coverage=<numerator>/<denominator>`, `grounded:brier=<numerator>/<denominator>`, `grounded:scorer=<id>@<revision>` and `knob:<name>=<value>`. Writes: the decision job store, through the `DecisionEval` job authority. Meristem producers of answers, topics and labels bind their own provenance. Caller chain: wire `Method::DecisionEval` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:126`) → `handle_decision_eval` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/jobs.rs:30`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_grounded_eval.rs::submit` → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_jobs.rs` → `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/jobs.rs`. Shape: files `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_grounded_eval.rs` (new); `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_jobs.rs` (existing); `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/jobs.rs` (existing); reuse `premises` in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:319`, adding premises with the weakest-class evidence rule. It asserts each refusal code and the readback of every binding. The test runs with tenant and principal context and adds one cross-tenant negative case. |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R135.7` | **Pre-plan test receipt gates pattern promotion.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints. Served operation `DecisionLog` with `RunRecord::CompiledProgram`. Code: new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/program_store/preplan.rs` with `PrePlanTestReceipt { tenant_id, run_id, repository_id, repository_revision, command_id, command_digest, started_at_ms, completed_at_ms, exit_code, artifact_manifest_digest, artifact_count, result_digest }` and `verify_preplan(receipt, plan_binding)`. The harness produces the receipt and Medulla verifies it. The harness stores the manifest through a blob-put port call before the commit. The commit rides the `DecisionLog` commit op. Add `reusable: bool`, `plan_binding: Option<PlanBinding>` (`{ repository_revision, command_digest, planned_at_ms }`, what the receipt must equal) and `preplan_receipt: Option<PrePlanTestReceipt>` to the `CompiledProgram` commit request, not to the stored program body. `verify_preplan(tenant_id, receipt, binding, manifest_reading, max_age_ms, policy_digest)` takes the Blob CAS reading (`ManifestReading`) from the handler, which reads it with `engine_manifest_length` in the caller's tenant namespace. A receipt of another tenant reads as missing. `completed_at_ms` must also be no more than the decision-policy knob `program.preplan_max_age_ms` (default 24 h, DE-R059.1-KNOBS) before `planned_at_ms`; older evidence is `PREPLAN_RECEIPT_STALE`. The promoted pattern is stored beside the program as `ReusablePattern` under `run_record/reusable_pattern/<task_signature>`, written in the commit that stores the program; `ProgramLookup` indexes it with `program.reusable` and receipt-digest premises. Rule: `tests_ran` is true only when the command digest and repository revision equal the plan binding and `completed_at_ms` precedes `planned_at_ms`. `artifacts_exist` is true only when `artifact_count` is positive and the manifest is readable in Blob CAS at `artifact_manifest_digest`. All digests are SHA-256 with 64 lowercase hex characters. A program may be marked reusable only when `exit_code` is zero and both booleans are true. The verifier returns both booleans, their evidence refs and the policy digest. Persist the pattern in the existing `CompiledProgram` model and index it through `ProgramLookup`. Add no second program store. R135.9 is retired into this row. Refusals: `PREPLAN_RECEIPT_MISSING`, `PREPLAN_COMMAND_MISMATCH`, `PREPLAN_RECEIPT_STALE`, `PREPLAN_ARTIFACTS_UNREADABLE`, `PREPLAN_ARTIFACTS_EMPTY`, `PREPLAN_TESTS_FAILED`. Each leaves the prior library unchanged. Evidence: `Claim` premises for the receipt fields and `Observation` for the Blob CAS read. Writes: `DecisionLog` only. Caller chain: wire `Method::DecisionLog` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:133`) → `handle_decision_log` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/log.rs:11`) → `stat_log::handle_log` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_log.rs:541`) → `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/program_store/preplan.rs`. Shape: files `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/program_store/preplan.rs` (new); reuse `stat_log::handle_log` dispatch in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_log.rs:541`. Depends: R135.2, R135.3. | Test: `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/program_store_tests.rs::preplan::reusable_pattern_requires_a_verified_preplan_receipt` (L3) promotes a pattern with valid evidence and asserts each refusal code. It also asserts independent readback of receipt, pattern and source trace refs, and a cross-tenant manifest reading as unreadable. |
Depends: MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R135.2, MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R135.3
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R106.1` | **Council positions coordinate into one evidence-bound decision.** Stage: 7 Conclude, served by `Decide` (kind `CouncilCoordination`). Medulla decides from what the caller pins in the request; it reads no store and no topology, so every check below is over request text and is deterministic. Types in new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/council.rs` (each `deny_unknown_fields`, declared in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision.rs`): `EvidenceRef { id: String, revision: u64, digest: String }`; `CouncilPosition { council_id: String, topology_revision: u64, position_id: String, persona_id: String, persona_revision: u64, option_id: String, claim_digest: String, evidence_refs: Vec<EvidenceRef>, constraint_refs: Vec<String> }`; `CouncilPolicy { policy_id: String, revision: u64, quorum_micros: u32 }`; `CouncilOutcome` closed `selected { option_id }`; `CouncilAbstention` closed `no_quorum`, `unresolved_conflict`; `CouncilResult { council_id: String, topology_revision: u64, input_position_ids: Vec<String>, accepted_position_ids: Vec<String>, rejected_position_ids: Vec<String>, outcome: Option<CouncilOutcome>, abstention: Option<CouncilAbstention>, policy_revision: u64, positions_digest: String, decision_digest: String }` with exactly one of `outcome` and `abstention` set. `positions_digest` is `Digest256::sha256(&serde_json::to_vec(&positions sorted by position_id)?).to_hex()`; `decision_digest` is `Digest256::sha256(&serde_json::to_vec(&(positions_digest, policy_id, policy_revision, outcome, abstention))?).to_hex()`. Request parameters (typed `TypedValue::Text` holding JSON, read by `text_param`, `int_param` and `json_param` of `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/support.rs`): `council_id` (text), `topology_revision` (int: the revision the caller says is current), `positions` (`Vec<CouncilPosition>`), `council_policy` (`CouncilPolicy`) and `evidence_current` (`Vec<EvidenceRef>`: the current head of every evidence id the caller holds). The one declared option is `council`, checked by `single_option`. Rule: `QuestionKind::CouncilCoordination` is added in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical.rs`; the family `CouncilFamily` in new `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/council.rs` is registered in `family::for_kind`. `constraints` refuses with `"<CODE>: detail"` (resolution kind `Constraint`) in this order: `COUNCIL_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` (no position, an empty id or digest, or a position whose `council_id` differs from the request's); `COUNCIL_DUPLICATE_POSITION` (two positions share `position_id` or `persona_id`); `COUNCIL_TOPOLOGY_MISMATCH` (a position's `topology_revision` differs from the request's); `COUNCIL_MISSING_EVIDENCE` (a position has no `evidence_refs`, or a ref id is absent from `evidence_current`); `COUNCIL_STALE_EVIDENCE` (a ref id is present there with another `revision` or `digest`); `COUNCIL_POLICY_REFUSED` (empty `policy_id`, `revision` 0, or `quorum_micros` below the `knob council.quorum_fraction` (`DecimalMicros`, default 500000, [500000, 1000000], unit fraction, `Tunable`, appended to the knob table of the council types file) or above 1000000). `conclude` counts positions per `option_id`. If the two highest counts are equal it abstains `COUNCIL_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT`. Otherwise the top option is selected only when `count * 1000000 > quorum_micros * positions`; else it abstains `COUNCIL_NO_QUORUM`. The abstentions go through `abstained(QuestionKind::CouncilCoordination, &CouncilRefusal)` of `support.rs`, with `CouncilRefusal` implementing `DecisionRefusal`. The answer option is `council_result:<json of CouncilResult>`; `accepted_position_ids` are the positions for the selected option and `rejected_position_ids` the rest, and an abstention accepts none. Refusals: the eight codes above in `pub const REFUSALS` of `council.rs`, collected by `codes_are_unique_and_stable` (R010.100.1). Evidence: premises `position:<id>`, `evidence:<id>@<revision>` and `council_policy:<id>@<revision>`; the weakest evidence class among the refs is the record class (a ref present in `evidence_current` with equal revision and digest is `Observation`, else the request is already refused). `Decide` writes nothing; `DecisionCommit` persists the record. Caller chain: wire `Method::Decide` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:112`) → `handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/statistical.rs:11`) → `stat_decide::handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:60`) → `decide_blocking` (`stat_decide.rs:132`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/council.rs` → `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical.rs` → `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/council.rs`. Shape: files `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/council.rs` (new); `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical.rs` (existing); `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/council.rs` (new); reuse `premises` in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:319`. It asserts each of the six request codes with `ResolutionKind::Constraint`, and `COUNCIL_STALE_EVIDENCE` against a changed digest in `evidence_current`. It asserts a cross-tenant refusal. `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/council.rs::tests::council_types_and_digests_round_trip` (L1) covers the round trip and both digests. |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R137.13` | **Measured signals select direct or recursive mode.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints; served operation `Decide`. Code: new file `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/recursion_mode.rs`. Add `QuestionKind::RecursionMode`. Add `ContextBudgetSignals { run_id, tool_output_bytes: u64, tool_output_digest, tool_call_ref, graph_snapshot_ref, graph_node_count: u64, observed_at_ms: u64, signal_digest }` to `crates/medulla-decision-outcome-types/src/decision/context_budget.rs`, carried as one JSON-text param `signals` (the outcome types cannot be a `TypedValue` variant), beside a `graph` text param naming the tenant graph the two refs are resolved in. Rule: the mode is `recursive` when either measure meets its threshold. `knob context.recursive_output_bytes` default 65536, [1024, 1073741824], bytes. `knob context.recursive_graph_nodes` default 50000, [100, 100000000], nodes. `knob context.signal_max_age_ms` default 60000, [1000, 3600000], ms. Cross-tenant means a ref does not resolve in the caller tenant: `tool_call_ref` and `graph_snapshot_ref` must each be a node of the row-level filtered tenant graph. Stale means `now - observed_at_ms` exceeds `context.signal_max_age_ms`. The digest is the SHA-256 digest of every other signal field. A run above both thresholds reports `OUTPUT_BYTES_AT_OR_ABOVE`. Invalid means a negative or missing value. Each is a request refusal with wire error `PARAMETER_INVALID`. Evidence: premises `recursion_mode.tool_output_bytes` and `recursion_mode.graph_node_count` (class Observation) and `recursion_mode.inputs_digest`. Writes: none; `Decide` is evaluate-only (AD-4). Each ref holds `record_id`, `outcome_revision` and `outcome_digest`. Authority: Medulla ranks and emits the tree. Rule: take the relevance of R134.4 for each visible skill of a task. `parent_skill_id` is the nearest retrieved ancestor named by the skill component's `parent` attribute. Context match is exact equality between the request's typed context-feature digest and the digest stored with a prior outcome (R020.1). When a skill has at least `knob skill_tree.min_outcomes` matching outcomes (default 5, [1, 1000], count), the score uses the outcome rate. Then `score = clamp(relevance + knob skill_tree.outcome_weight * (success_rate - 0.5), 0, 1)`. The knob `outcome_weight` defaults to 0.3 ([0, 1], fraction). Below that support the score is the relevance alone. Keep at most `knob skill_tree.max_nodes` skills per task (default 8, [1, 32], count). Rank by score descending, then skill id ascending. The tree is sealed on the record as `skill_trees` and bound into the record digest. A prior outcome is a stored evaluation, with a recorded success or failure, of a record of the caller's own tenant and principal whose sealed context digest equals the request's context digest; it counts for the skill named by the evaluation's `selected_agent`. The context digest ignores `outcome_pins`. `outcome_revision` is the record's evaluation count and `outcome_digest` covers every stored evaluation of the record. The request may carry `outcome_pins` (`SkillPlanQuery`, at most 64 refs); when present exactly the pinned records feed the tree and each must equal its stored outcome, so a plan is reproducible. A node cites at most 64 refs, newest records first. Only skills at or above `knob skill_plan.relevance_floor` are nodes. The three `skill_tree.*` knobs are declared beside the `skill_plan.*` knobs in `knob_families/task_plan.rs`. The ranked trees are the `skill_trees` field of `TaskPlan`; the plan digest covers them. Outcome feedback changes later breadth only through R140.102. Refusals: `SKILL_TREE_CYCLE`, `SKILL_PARENT_UNKNOWN`, `STALE_OUTCOME_EVIDENCE` (a ref whose digest differs from the stored outcome). Evidence: one `Claim` premise per node with `skill_node:task=<id>;skill=<id>;parent=<id>;rank=<n>;score_q32=<n>`, and the knob premises. Writes: none. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R134.11` | **Horizon partition and credit checkpoints.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints. Served operation `Decide` with `QuestionKind::TaskPlan`, then `DecisionLog` for checkpoints. Code: new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/task_plan/horizon.rs` with `HorizonPartition`, `HorizonCheckpoint` and `partition_horizons(plan, knobs)`. Authority: Medulla partitions and verifies checkpoints. Rule: layer the canonical plan by dependency depth. Close a horizon at the last layer boundary that keeps it within `knob horizon.max_steps` (default 8, [1, 64], steps). A single layer wider than the knob forms its own horizon. A dependency component that has no layer boundary to split at refuses. `HorizonPartition { plan_digest, horizons: Vec<{ index, step_ids }>, credit_ceiling }`. The ceiling is `knob horizon.credit_ceiling` (default 200000, [1000, 10000000], tokens). `HorizonCheckpoint { plan_digest, horizon_index, consumed, reserved, remaining, ceiling, rule }` uses `u64`. The fixed accounting rule is `consumed + reserved + remaining == ceiling`, checked with overflow detection. The partition is an optional `horizons` field on `TaskPlan`. A plan within the limit yields one horizon. A checkpoint is stored through `DecisionLog` as `RunRecord::HorizonCheckpoint { plan, policy, checkpoint }` (`DecisionLogOp::RunRecord`, R135.3) under the key `run_record/horizon_checkpoint/<plan_digest>/<index>`. The commit re-derives the plan's partition under `policy` (a plan whose digest or horizons do not re-derive is stale), validates the checkpoint with `check_horizon_checkpoint` before the write and refuses horizon n > 0 until horizon n - 1 is stored. The served plan always carries `horizons`, attached by `attach_horizons` after the critical chain; `partition.plan_digest` is the plan digest before the partition is attached. A plan with more steps than `horizon.max_steps` and a single layer refuses `HORIZON_UNSPLITTABLE` (unreachable through `plan_explicit_tasks`, which needs every step to feed the output; reachable on a hand-built body). Refusals: `HORIZON_UNSPLITTABLE`, `HORIZON_BUDGET_RULE_INVALID`, `HORIZON_OVER_CREDIT`, `HORIZON_CHECKPOINT_MISSING`, `HORIZON_PLAN_STALE`. Evidence: one `Claim` premise per horizon with `horizon:index=<n>;steps=<ids>`. Writes: `Decide` writes nothing; `DecisionLog` writes checkpoints. Caller chain: wire `Method::Decide` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:112`) → `handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/statistical.rs:11`) → `stat_decide::handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:60`) → `decide_blocking` (`stat_decide.rs:132`) → the family `decide` entry registered in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/mod.rs` → `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/task_plan/horizon.rs`. Shape: files `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/task_plan/horizon.rs` (new); reuse the sibling closed types in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical.rs` and the executor `execute` in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_executor.rs:220`. A long plan splits at layer boundaries. It asserts exact reconciliation of a logged checkpoint, each refusal code, and a cross-tenant checkpoint never satisfying the check. |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R134.12` | **Behavior: width and depth rung choice.** Stage: 6 Statistical rank. Served operation `Decide` with new `QuestionKind::TrajectoryLadder`. Code: new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/trajectory_ladder.rs` (types), `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/trajectory_ladder.rs` (kernel `choose_rung`) and `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/trajectory_ladder.rs`. Authority: Medulla selects width and depth. Request `TrajectoryLadderRequest { task_digest, input_snapshot_digest, max_width, rungs: Vec<{ rung_id, width, depth }>, improvement_claim: Option<rung_id> }` carried as the JSON `ladder` parameter; an `improvement_claim` is answered only when a stored paired verdict of R134.12.1 has that rung as winner `arm` on the same snapshot, else `TRAJECTORY_IMPROVEMENT_UNPROVEN`; `max_width` is the permitted K upper bound of R140.100. Rule: a rung is legal when `width <= max_width`. It must also satisfy `depth <= knob trajectory.max_depth` (default 3, [1, 8], levels). The rung set must contain the baseline `width 1, depth 1`. Policy supplies the legal set. A fitted head never widens it. With a promoted head (AD-10), the head ranks legal rungs: a `WeightedFeatures` head with two weights over the standardised features `[width, depth]`, highest Q32 score first, ties to the smaller rung in the order below. A head not of that shape refuses `HEAD_INVALID`. Without one, `knob trajectory.default_rung` (default 0, [0, 15], index) picks the legal rung at that index. The order is `width * depth`, then width, then depth, then rung id. Index 0 is the smallest rung. An index past the last legal rung picks the last one. The result lists the chosen rung and ordered trajectory ids `<decision_digest_prefix>-t<k>` for k from 1 to width; the prefix is the first 12 hex characters of the digest of the task digest, the input snapshot digest and the chosen rung id. It names the baseline id. Refusals: `TRAJECTORY_NO_LEGAL_RUNG`, `TRAJECTORY_BASELINE_MISSING`, `TRAJECTORY_IMPROVEMENT_UNPROVEN`. Evidence: premises `trajectory_rung:id=<id>;width=<n>;depth=<n>`, the head digest when one ranked, and the knob premises. Writes: none. These append-only children preserve the existing parent contracts named below. All remain SPECIFIED. This definition records planned acceptance and does not claim implementation or served receipts.

| ID | Requirement | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R042.100` | **RETIRED: duplicate of MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R159.** `PathPreference` already owns path outcome history and the skip rule, and the SDK consumes only R159. | Retired; see MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R159. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R042.101` | **RETIRED: Duplicates the tool-necessity root R165.** R165 owns the per-model necessity measurement, the comparison and the mismatch trace record. | Retired; see MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R165. |
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R129.100` | **Versioned rule lifecycle from correction to revocation.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints, op `DecisionLog` with new `ProposeRule`, `ApproveRule` and `RevokeRule`. Code: `RuleLifecycle { Proposed, Active, Superseded, Revoked }` and `RuleVersion` in `crates/medulla-agent-types/src/agent_guardrail.rs`. `RuleVersion { rule_id, version, scope, source_output_digest, predecessor, state, approver, approver_second }` binds the correction to its run output. `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_rule_promotion.rs` serves the three ops. Rule: a proposal stays `Proposed` until approval and the R129.3 gate both pass; invariant compliance never replaces approval. Activation supersedes the declared predecessor in one write. Revocation names the active version and keeps history. Approval needs two distinct approvers (`Fixed`): the approver is the verified caller, the first `ApproveRule` records `approver` and leaves the version `Proposed`, and the second, from a different principal and naming the same `source_output_digest`, runs the invariant gate, publishes the `GuardrailRule` and activates. The same approver twice refuses `RULE_APPROVER_NOT_DISTINCT`; an approval naming another `source_output_digest` than the one the version was proposed with (`RuleVersion.source_output_digest`, stored in the proposal row; no other record is consulted) refuses `RULE_OUTPUT_MISMATCH`, and `RuleVersion.version` is a `u64` counting the proposals of one rule id from 1. `RevokeRule` retires only that version's revision of the published `GuardrailRule` component (DECIDED: retirement is per revision, not per component): it publishes a new revision of the same component id carrying the attribute `revision_status = retired` (`REVISION_STATUS_ATTRIBUTE`, `is_revision_retired` in `crates/medulla-agent-types/src/agent_guardrail.rs`) with a content digest of its own, before it writes its `Revoked` transition row, and a retry that finds the head revision already retired only writes the row; `published_guardrail_rules` (so `GuardrailEntailment`) and the best-practice projection leave a retired revision out, so a revoked rule is no longer entailed, and a later version approved for the same rule id publishes a new revision over it and is entailed. The component-level tombstone (`retire_component`, terminal) is not used for a revoke. Storage is append-only: the proposal row `rule-version:<rule_id>:<version>` and one `RuleTransition` row `rule-transition:<rule_id>:<sequence>` per step, and activation writes its `Active` and the predecessor's `Superseded` rows in one `put_decision_artifacts` call. The Python senders `propose_rule_op`, `approve_rule_op`, `revoke_rule_op` and `promote_rule_op` are in `medulla/decision_client.py`. `crates/medulla-mutation-types/src/rule_correction.rs` is deleted (it had no caller). Refusals: `RULE_OUTPUT_MISMATCH`, `RULE_PREDECESSOR_STALE`, `RULE_NOT_ACTIVE` and `RULE_APPROVER_NOT_DISTINCT`. Evidence: each transition stores actor, version and source-output digest. Writes: `DecisionLog` only. Caller chain: wire `Method::DecisionLog` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:133`) → `handle_decision_log` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/log.rs:11`) → `stat_log::handle_log` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_log.rs:541`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_rule_promotion.rs` → `crates/medulla-mutation-types/src/rule_correction.rs` → `crates/medulla-agent-types/src/agent_guardrail.rs`. Shape: files `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_rule_promotion.rs` (new); `crates/medulla-mutation-types/src/rule_correction.rs` (existing); `crates/medulla-agent-types/src/agent_guardrail.rs` (existing); reuse `stat_log::handle_log` dispatch in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_log.rs:541`. Depends: R129.5. | Test: `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/rule_promotion_tests.rs::rule_versions_move_through_approval_supersession_and_revocation` (L3) asserts each state, each code, revoke v2 then approve v3 and v3 entailed, and a cross-tenant refusal. |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R134.100` | **Fan-out aggregation decision.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints then 7 Conclude. Served operation `Decide` with new `QuestionKind::FanoutAggregate`. Code: new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/task_plan/fanout.rs` (`FanoutAggregateRequest`, `FanoutSubtaskResult`, `FanoutAggregate`, pure `aggregate_fanout`) and `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/fanout_aggregate.rs`. Add `TypedValue::FanoutResults(Box<FanoutAggregateRequest>)`. Authority: Medulla applies the plan's already-selected `AggregationOp` to the complete receipt set. It adds no fan-out width, concurrency policy or second aggregation authority. Arbora `agents.run` owns durable instance receipts and capacity refusals (`ARBORA-FLEET-R024.5`). Request: `plan_digest`, the plan's `aggregation` (`op` and `reducer_id`), `expected_task_ids`, and per subtask `{ task_id, status, result_digest, receipt_id, receipt_digest, failure_gap }` with `status` either `ok` or `failed`. Rule: the result set must equal `expected_task_ids` exactly once each. `concat` returns the ok digests in canonical task order. `majority_vote` returns the most frequent ok digest and breaks ties by the lowest task id carrying it. `first_valid` returns the first ok digest in task-id order. `reduce` returns the ordered ok digests and the `reducer_id`. The harness runs the reducer. `aggregate_digest` is a SHA-256 digest (64 lowercase hex characters) over the operator, the ordered `(task_id, status, result_digest or gap)` entries and the plan digest. Independent readback uses `DecisionLogOp::Get`, then recomputes `aggregate_digest`. Refusals: `FANOUT_CHILD_MISSING`, `FANOUT_CHILD_DUPLICATE`, `FANOUT_CHILD_UNKNOWN`, `FANOUT_PLAN_MISMATCH` (the plan digest is not 64 lowercase hex characters, or `reducer_id` is not present exactly for `reduce`), `FANOUT_NO_VALID_RESULT`. Evidence: one `Claim` premise per result `fanout_result:task=<id>;status=<s>;receipt=<id>`, one `Definition` premise per canonical entry `fanout_entry:task=<id>;status=<s>;value=<digest or gap>`, and one `Definition` premise `fanout_aggregate:op=<op>;plan=<digest>;aggregate_digest=<digest>`. Each result `receipt_id` must be a node the caller's row-level filtered graph (the `graph` parameter) returns for the caller's tenant; a receipt in another tenant, a hidden one and a missing one refuse identically with `FANOUT_CHILD_UNKNOWN` before the operator runs. An ok result without a 64-hex `result_digest` and a failed result without a `failure_gap` refuse `FANOUT_CHILD_MISSING`. Writes: none. Caller chain: wire `Method::Decide` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:112`) → `handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/statistical.rs:11`) → `stat_decide::handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:60`) → `decide_blocking` (`stat_decide.rs:132`) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/fanout_aggregate.rs` → `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/task_plan/fanout.rs`. Shape: files `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/fanout_aggregate.rs` (new); `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/task_plan/fanout.rs` (new); reuse the sibling closed types in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical.rs` and the executor `execute` in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_executor.rs:220`. It asserts each refusal code, an independent `Get` readback that recomputes the digest, and a cross-tenant receipt refusing identically to a missing one. |

Code: family `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/paper_admission.rs`. Candidates are staged paper nodes in a graph source. Caller-supplied or model-supplied scores enter only as claims, never as relevance. Each admitted paper lists the claim ids from text `paper.claim_ids` as its selected claims. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R140.100` | **Complexity-gated K-trajectory decision.** Stage: 7 Conclude, family `TaskPlan`, served operation `Decide`. Code: `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/task_plan/trajectory_budget.rs` holds `TrajectoryBudgetRequest`, `TrajectoryBudget`, `ComplexityFeature`, `ComplexityScorer` and `fn decide_budget`. Request: `task_digest`, ordered features, an optional `requested_k` and one scorer (a request without a scorer refuses `TRAJECTORY_POLICY_ABSENT`). The decision is `TrajectoryBudget { branch, score_micro, k_min, k_max, k, decision_digest }`; an absent `requested_k` selects the largest permitted K. `decide_budget(request, knobs, now_ms)` is pure: the caller supplies the knobs and the clock. A feature has `id`, `value` in integer micro-units, `unit`, `source_ref`, `source_revision`, `source_digest` and `observed_at_ms`. The scorer has `id`, `revision`, `digest` and one `weight` per feature in micro-units; a weight with no feature, or a feature with no weight, refuses `TRAJECTORY_FEATURE_MISSING`. The engine recomputes the scorer digest as SHA-256 over canonical bytes. Score = sum of value times weight, divided by 1000000, in 128-bit integer math. The branch is complex when score reaches `knob trajectory.complexity_threshold` (default 1000000, range [0, 1000000000000], unit micro-score). A simple branch returns K=1. A complex branch returns permitted K in `[2, knob trajectory.max_k]` (default 8, range [2, 64], unit trajectories). A feature is stale when `observed_at_ms` is older than `knob trajectory.feature_max_age` (default 3600, range [1, 604800], unit seconds). Refusals: `TRAJECTORY_FEATURE_MISSING`, `TRAJECTORY_FEATURE_STALE`, `TRAJECTORY_SCORER_UNPINNED`, `TRAJECTORY_POLICY_ABSENT` and `TRAJECTORY_K_INVALID` for a requested K outside the branch range. Request: per source trajectory `run_id`, `candidate_id`, `source_revision`, `trace_digest`, `trace_token_len`, removed ranges and retained ranges. A range is half-open `[start, end)` in `u64` token offsets with start below end. The request also names the redaction policy and the tokenizer, each as a pin with id and revision. Each source revision and digest must match the tenant-visible outcome record read through `LogReader`; the caller passes those records to `validate_projection(request, stored)` as a map keyed by run id, so the function stays pure. Any overlap among the ranges of one source, removed or retained, is refused. The engine shuffles the ordered source ids with Fisher-Yates. The random stream is ChaCha8, seeded by SHA-256 of the seed bytes. The new candidate id is SHA-256 over the sorted parent digests and the decision digest. It has 64 lowercase hex characters. Code: types in the new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/memory_rewrite.rs`; kernel in the new `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/memory_rewrite.rs`. `MemoryRewriteProposal` holds `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `idempotency_key` and `record_id`. The record id names a `MemoryRecord`. It holds `active` and `candidate`, each a `RevisionRef` with `revision` and `digest`. It also holds `active_signals`, `candidate_signals`, `token_count`, `metric_id`, `graph` (the graph whose snapshot store holds the record's head, read behind the caller's read access), `policy` (the digest of the decision policy the proposal was made under) and `policy_ref` (the `DecisionPolicyRef` that resolves it; the resolved digest must equal `policy`) and `history`. `history` holds at most 50 `HistoryEntry` items (`revision`, `fidelity_q4`) and a `history_digest`. Digests are SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex characters. `MemoryRewriteEvaluation` holds all inputs, `fidelity_q4`, `signal_count`, `token_count`, `signal_per_token_q4`, `verdict` (`Admit` or `Discard`), `reason_codes` and `receipt_digest`. Rule: the kernel normalizes each signal (NFC, lower case, collapsed whitespace) and hashes it. `fidelity` is `|S_active ∩ S_candidate| / |S_active|` over those hashes, rounded half to even to 4 decimals and stored as `fidelity_q4` in [0, 10000]. `signal_per_token` is `signal_count / token_count` with `signal_count` the number of distinct candidate signals, also rounded to 4 decimals. `metric_id` must name an entry of the code table `MEMORY_FIDELITY_METRICS`. Its only entry is `memory_fidelity_set_overlap`, revision 1, with the SHA-256 of its specification text. Verdict: `Discard` with every reason that applies, in this order: `FIDELITY_BELOW_MIN`, `SIGNAL_EFFICIENCY_BELOW_MIN` or `DEGRADATION_RULE_TRIGGERED`; otherwise `Admit`. The degradation rule triggers when at least `knob memory_rewrite.max_degradations` of the last `knob memory_rewrite.history_window` history entries have a `fidelity_q4` below the minimum. Knobs, decision-policy knobs declared in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/memory_rewrite.rs` and registered in `knob_families::REGISTRY` (DECISIONS DE-R059.1-KNOBS), read by `MemoryRewriteKnobs::from_policy`: `knob memory_rewrite.min_fidelity` default 0.95, range [0.5, 1], unit ratio. `knob memory_rewrite.min_signal_per_token` default 0.02, range [0, 1], unit signals per token. `knob memory_rewrite.history_window` default 5, range [1, 50], unit rewrites. `knob memory_rewrite.max_degradations` default 2, range [0, 50], unit rewrites. Refusals, in the `memory_change` family table: `MEMORY_METRIC_UNRESOLVED`, `MEMORY_POLICY_MISSING`, `MEMORY_HISTORY_MISSING` (no history digest, or a digest that does not match the entries), `MEMORY_TOKEN_DENOMINATOR_ZERO`, `MEMORY_ACTIVE_SIGNALS_EMPTY`, `MEMORY_REVISION_STALE` (active revision differs from the stored head). Evidence premises: `memory:record=<id>`, `memory:active=<digest>`, `memory:candidate=<digest>`, `memory:metric=<id>@<revision>`, `memory:fidelity_q4=<n>`, `memory:signal_per_token_q4=<n>`, `memory:policy=<digest>` and `knob:<name>=<value>`. Writes: none in the kernel; the receipt is written by the `DecisionEval` job authority. A `Discard` keeps the active revision. Depends: R617.1, R010.100.1, R179.1, MEDULLA-DURABLE-KERNEL-R085.2. Caller chain: `Method::DecisionEval` -> `handle_decision_eval` (crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/jobs.rs:30) -> `handle_eval` (crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_jobs.rs:877) -> `serve_eval` (:609) -> `MemoryRewriteSubmit` arm (R141.102) -> `evaluate_rewrite(proposal, knobs, stored_head_revision) -> Result<MemoryRewriteEvaluation, RefusalCode>` (the caller reads the stored head revision; refusals are checked in the order the codes are listed). Shape: `MemoryRewriteProposal` in new crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/memory_rewrite.rs; pure kernel in new crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/memory_rewrite.rs; reuse the digest helper of digest.rs; no store access in the kernel. | Test: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/memory_rewrite.rs::tests::fidelity_is_set_overlap_rounded_half_to_even` (planned) (L1) asserts exact fidelity values and each refusal. Verified by the root slice test `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/memory_change_tests.rs::rewrite_admit_and_discard_through_decision_eval` (planned) (L3), which also asserts that a `Discard` leaves the active digest unchanged. |
