| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R141.101` | **Memory-change benchmark receipt.** Stage: 10 Learn, served by `DecisionEval` (wired in R141.102). Code: types in the new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/memory_benchmark.rs`; kernel in the new `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/memory_benchmark.rs`. `MemoryChangeBenchmarkRequest` holds `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `idempotency_key`, `record_id` and `change_kind`. The change kind is the `ChangeKind` of R141.104. It holds `baseline` and `candidate`, each a `RevisionRef`. It holds `dataset` with id, revision, digest and queries. It also holds `k`, `evaluator_revision`, `policy` and two `RunResults` (`baseline_results`, `candidate_results`), one per side; each `RunResults` names the `RevisionRef` it was measured on. `MEMORY_SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH` is a run measured on another revision than the request names; `MEMORY_REVISION_STALE` is a candidate revision not newer than the baseline revision; `MEMORY_METRIC_UNRESOLVED` is a `k` of zero or above `memory_change.max_k`, or a knob that does not resolve to its declared type. `RevisionRef` and `ChangeKind` are declared in `memory_benchmark.rs` of the types crate. The ratios are decimal-micro knobs, and the discard reasons are returned together in the order recall, accuracy, regression. Each query holds `query_id`, `expected_evidence_ids` (non-empty) and `reference_answer_digest`. Each `RunResults` entry holds `query_id`, `top_ids` and `answer_text`. Rule: per query, `recall_ppm` is `|expected ∩ top_k| / |expected|` in parts per million, rounded half to even. `recall_at_k` is the sum of `recall_ppm` over queries divided by the query count, rounded half to even. An answer is correct when the SHA-256 of its normalized text (NFC, lower case, collapsed whitespace) equals `reference_answer_digest`. `answer_accuracy` is `correct / queries`, rounded the same way. Admit when the candidate metrics reach `knob memory_change.min_recall` and `knob memory_change.min_answer_accuracy`, and neither falls below the baseline by more than `knob memory_change.max_regression`. Otherwise `Discard`, with the reason code `RECALL_BELOW_MIN`, `ACCURACY_BELOW_MIN` or `REGRESSION_ABOVE_MAX`. Knobs: `knob memory_change.min_recall` default 0.8, range [0, 1], unit ratio. `knob memory_change.min_answer_accuracy` default 0.8, range [0, 1], unit ratio. `knob memory_change.max_regression` default 0, range [0, 0.1], unit ratio. `knob memory_change.max_k` default 100, range [1, 1000], unit items. Refusals, in the `memory_change` family table: `MEMORY_DATASET_EMPTY`, `MEMORY_EXPECTED_MISSING`, `MEMORY_COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE` (a run misses a query), `MEMORY_SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH`, `MEMORY_METRIC_UNRESOLVED`, `MEMORY_REVISION_STALE`. Evidence premises: `memory:dataset=<digest>`, `memory:recall_ppm=<numerator>/<denominator>`, `memory:accuracy=<correct>/<queries>`, `memory:baseline=<digest>`, `memory:candidate=<digest>` and `knob:<name>=<value>`. Writes: none in the kernel; the `DecisionEval` job authority writes the receipt. Depends: R141.100. Caller chain: `Method::DecisionEval` -> `handle_decision_eval` (crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/jobs.rs:30) -> `handle_eval` (crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_jobs.rs:877) -> `serve_eval` (:609) -> `MemoryChangeBenchmarkSubmit` arm (R141.102) -> the benchmark kernel. Shape: `MemoryChangeBenchmarkRequest` in new crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/memory_benchmark.rs; pure kernel in new crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/memory_benchmark.rs; `ChangeKind` from R141.104. | Test: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/memory_benchmark.rs::tests::recall_and_accuracy_use_exact_counts` (planned) (L1) asserts numerators, positive denominators and each failed metric blocking admission on its own. Verified by the root slice test `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/memory_change_tests.rs::benchmark_receipt_binds_both_snapshots` (planned) (L3). |

`pub struct LocalCertificationBody { pub schema_version: u16, pub skill: ComponentDependency, pub classification: SkillClassification, pub dependencies: Vec<ComponentDependency>, pub pins: LocalSkillPins, pub run_id: String, pub results: Vec<CriterionResult>, pub completion_revision: u64 }` (`results` sorted by `criterion_id`); `pub struct LocalCertificationAttestation { pub body: LocalCertificationBody, pub digest: String }`. Digest: `digest: String` is `digest_text(LOCAL_CERTIFICATION_DIGEST_DOMAIN, &body)` of `medulla_query_types::solve_scalar`, the one decision digest scheme of `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/digest.rs` (`sha256(domain ‖ 0x00 ‖ compact JSON in field order)`, rendered `sha256:<hex>`); the constant `pub const LOCAL_CERTIFICATION_DIGEST_DOMAIN: &str = "eg/local-certification/v1";` is added to `digest.rs` beside `DECISION_POLICY_DIGEST_DOMAIN`. Then it returns the attestation with sorted results and its digest. The job stores the attestation by digest; the job is the write authority. The call is idempotent on the digests of skill, model, dataset and criteria. A workflow request needs one stored attestation per named atomic dependency. Its skill pin must equal the skill currently published in the `AgentLibraryStore`. Its model and criteria pins must equal the request pins. Any edit of skill, model, dataset or criteria revision makes the stored attestation stale. Refusals, registered in the `REFUSALS` table: `CERT_RECEIPT_MISMATCH`, `CERT_CRITERIA_INCOMPLETE`, `CERT_CRITERION_FAILED`, `CERT_ATOMIC_HAS_DEPENDENCIES`, `CERT_WORKFLOW_NO_DEPENDENCIES`, `CERT_DEPENDENCY_MISSING` and `CERT_DEPENDENCY_STALE`. A refusal stores nothing. Evidence: the attestation lists `skill`, `model`, `dataset`, `criteria`, `receipt` and `criterion:<id>` entries. The class is `Observation`, because the admin-only op authenticates the submitting principal; a job output has no evidence-class field, so the premises are `premises: Vec<String>` on `LocalCertificationAttestation`, outside its digest (the attestation digest covers the pins and criteria only). A dependency's stored attestation is current only when its skill pin equals the request's dependency pin and the latest published revision of that component in the `AgentLibraryStore`, and its model, dataset and criteria pins equal the request's; attestations are found by scanning the tenant's `local_certification/` artifact rows. The op is mirrored in the Python client and models in the same change (`medulla/generated`, including the missing sibling ranking and grounded evaluation ops, which the generator emits together). Depends: R142.100. Shape: new crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_certification.rs; attestations stored by digest in the `AgentLibraryStore` the job already holds; reuse `submit_job` (stat_jobs.rs:514) for idempotency. | Test: `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/certification_tests.rs::attests_atomic_and_gates_workflow` (planned) (L3) asserts the attestation, each refusal code, no store write on refusal and one cross-tenant negative case. |
Depends: MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R142.100
| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R142.102` | **Certification hot-path proof.** Stage: 10 Learn, served operation `DecisionEval`. The root adds a `DecisionEval` arm, so the generated client gains `certify_local_skill`. The L4 test runs over a loopback engine with authentication. It submits a matching atomic receipt and reads the attestation by digest. It then submits a workflow that needs the attestation, changes the skill revision and checks refusal. The job path is not a hot path, so no benchmark group exists. Arbora and Meristem checks live in their own specs. Depends: R142.101. The digest is SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex characters. `IndexlessBudget` holds `max_rows`, `max_visits` and `max_cost_units`, all `u64`. `CostReport` holds `rows_visited`, `visits`, `cost_used`, `remaining` (an `IndexlessBudget`), `applied_budget`, `operation_ids` and `authorization_revision`. `IndexlessRequest` holds `tenant_id`, `graph`, `ops` (1 to 64), `budget` (optional) and `policy`. `IndexlessResult` holds `rows` and `cost`. Rule: `RawRead` returns one document's text. `CorpusScan` enumerates `Document` nodes in id order. `VerifySpan` checks that `[start_byte, end_byte)` lies on UTF-8 character boundaries and that the SHA-256 of the slice equals `expected_digest`. Costs per unit: `knob indexless.read_cost` default 1, range [1, 100], unit cost units per document. `knob indexless.scan_cost` default 1, range [1, 100], unit cost units per row. `knob indexless.verify_cost` default 2, range [1, 100], unit cost units per span. Rule: before each operation, the meter computes the rows, visits and cost that the operation needs. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R100.100.1` | **Ranking evaluation request and hits-at-k kernel.** Stage: 10 Learn, served by `DecisionEval`. Code: new types in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/ranking_eval.rs`; new kernel in `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/ranking_eval.rs`. `PinnedSet` holds `id`, `revision` and `digest` (SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex characters). `LabelSet` is a `PinnedSet` plus `pairs`, each pair a `query_id` and a relevant `doc_id`. `RetrievalRankingRequest` holds `tenant_id`, `idempotency_key`, `corpus`, `labels`, `queries` (a `PinnedSet` plus the query id list), `k`, `evaluator_revision` and `algorithms`. Each `AlgorithmRun` holds `algorithm_id`, `version`, `settings_digest`, `corpus_digest`, `input_digest` and one `QueryRanking` per query (`query_id`, `ranked_ids`). The output of `SynthesizeSearchTask` is an accepted source of `PinnedSet` items. Rule: `hits_at_k(labels, queries, run, k)` returns `HitsAtK { numerator, denominator }`. The numerator counts queries whose first `k` ranked ids include a relevant id. The denominator is the query count. The value is `numerator / denominator` as parts per million, rounded half to even, in a field named `value_ppm`. Knobs: `knob ranking_eval.max_k` default 1000, range [10, 10000], unit items. `knob ranking_eval.min_algorithms` default 2, range [2, 16], unit algorithms. `knob ranking_eval.max_queries` default 10000, range [100, 100000], unit queries. The kernel recomputes the digest of each pinned set from its content and compares it with the bound digest. Refusals live in the new `retrieval_eval` family table and as `StatisticalErrorCode` variants. They are `RANKING_QUERY_SET_EMPTY`, `RANKING_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, `RANKING_K_OUT_OF_RANGE` and `RANKING_ALGORITHMS_TOO_FEW`. `RANKING_LABELS_MISSING` means a query has no pair. `RANKING_CORPUS_DRIFT` means a run reports another corpus digest. `RANKING_RESULTS_INCOMPLETE` means a run misses a query. `RANKING_SETTINGS_MISMATCH` means a run input digest differs from the request input digest. Writes: none in the kernel. Depends: R010.100.1, R179.1. Shape: types in new crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/ranking_eval.rs declared in statistical.rs; the three knobs in new crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/knob_families/ranking_eval.rs (`RankingEvalKnobs::from_policy` resolves them); pure kernel in new crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/ranking_eval.rs (`hits_at_k`, `check_request`, `evaluate_ranking`); a query set above `ranking_eval.max_queries` refuses `RANKING_QUERY_SET_TOO_LARGE`; `LabelSet::content_digest` and `QuerySet::content_digest` are order-independent SHA-256 digests over the sorted content, and `RetrievalRankingRequest::input_digest` is the digest every run echoes. | Test: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/ranking_eval.rs::tests::hits_at_k_counts_queries_with_a_relevant_top_k_item` (L1) checks exact numerators and denominators for two runs and each refusal code. Verified by the root slice test `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/retrieval_eval_tests.rs::ranking_evaluation_is_sealed_and_readable` (L3). |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R100.100.3` | **Context search model and offset kernel.** Stage: 1 Visibility, read path served by `RetrievalContextSearch`. Code: types in the new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/context_search.rs`; kernel in the new `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/context_search.rs`. Add `unicode-normalization` (already in `Cargo.lock`) to `crates/medulla-decision-stats/Cargo.toml` under the `decision` feature. `RetrievalContextSearchRequest` holds `tenant_id`, `graph`, `query`, `ngram_n`, `max_spans` and `cursor`. `ContextSpan` holds `document_id`, `document_revision`, `text_digest`, `match_start`, `match_end`, `context_start`, `context_end` and `context_text`. `RetrievalContextSearchResult` holds `spans`, `query_revision`, `index_digest`, `authorization_revision` and `next_cursor`. Rule: the stored text is the original UTF-8 string of a node of type `Document` in its `text` property. The kernel normalizes it to NFC and builds a map `norm_to_orig` of ranges. The kernel splits the original at each character with combining class 0. It normalizes each segment and records the original byte range of that segment. `validate_map` must prove that ranges are ordered, cover the text, lie on character boundaries and stay within the original length. A match is an exact normalized substring of one query n-gram, joined with single spaces. The public offsets are half-open byte offsets in the original text and always address `text_digest`. `context_*` offsets extend each match by `knob context_search.context_bytes` default 160, range [0, 4096], unit bytes, then snap to character boundaries. Other knobs: `knob context_search.ngram_n` default 2, range [1, 8], unit tokens. `knob context_search.max_spans` default 100, range [1, 1000], unit spans. `knob context_search.max_span_bytes` default 8192, range [1024, 65536], unit bytes. `index_digest` is the SHA-256 (64 lowercase hex characters) of the normalized text plus the map. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R100.100.4` | **Context search method, authorization and served proof.** Stage: 1 Visibility, served by the new read method `Method::RetrievalContextSearch`. Code: add the variant `RetrievalContextSearch { request: Box<RetrievalContextSearchRequest> }` in `crates/medulla-protocol-types/src/protocol/method/method_03.rs`, next to `Discover`. Classify it as a read in `crates/medulla-server-auth/src/access/read_classification.rs`. The handler is the new `crates/medulla-h-query/src/query/context_search.rs`, routed from `crates/medulla-h-query/src/query/dispatch.rs`. Arbora serves it as an `eg.*` operation without a new row. Rule: the handler reads `Document` nodes from the row-level-security filtered snapshot of the named graph. It filters by visibility before it matches, counts or builds a cursor. The cursor is opaque. It encodes the tenant, the query digest, the snapshot revision and the next offset, with a SHA-256 check value. A changed snapshot revision makes the cursor stale. A span reader never returns more than `knob context_search.max_spans` spans per call or `knob context_search.max_span_bytes` bytes per span. Refusals: `CONTEXT_CURSOR_STALE`, `CONTEXT_CURSOR_INVALID` and the kernel codes of R100.100.3. A denied document yields no span, no count and no offset. The response equals the one for an absent document. Evidence: the result names `query_revision`, `index_digest` and `authorization_revision`. The request carries `policy` (a `DecisionPolicyRef`, default the engine policy); the handler resolves it through the decision-policy seam (a pinned policy is read from the Agent Library of the verified tenant) and reads the four `context_search.*` knobs from the resolved policy, so a request never exceeds them: `max_spans` per call is the smaller of the request value and the knob (0 takes the knob), and `ngram_n` of 0 takes the knob while any other width must lie in the knob's range. The request `tenant_id` must equal the verified tenant (`ACCESS_DENIED`) and `graph` must be the graph the call targets (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`). `document_revision` is the revision of the snapshot the text was read at, and `authorization_revision` is the verified caller's authorization revision (agent and sorted scopes). `index_digest` covers the visible documents only, in document-id order. Writes: none. Depends: R100.100.3. Caller chain: `Method::RetrievalContextSearch` (new variant, R100.100.4) -> the query router `try_handle` (crates/medulla-h-query/src/query/dispatch.rs:9) -> new `crates/medulla-h-query/src/query/context_search.rs`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R154.1` | **Model.** Stage: 6 rank; operations `MemoryRemember` and `MemoryRecall`. Extend `pub const KNOBS: &[KnobSpec]` of the `memory` family in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/knob_families/memory.rs` (DECISIONS DE-R154.1: one table, in the decision plane). It lists every memory parameter and no other. Admission: a `MemoryRecord` enters when it carries a tenant. Its size must be at most `knob memory.entry_max_bytes`. The tenant total must stay at most `knob memory.tenant_max_bytes`: the total is the sum of the stored node bytes of the tenant's `memory:<tenant>:` nodes, kept as a durable per-tenant counter node `memory-quota:<tenant>` (type `MemoryTenantUsage`, properties `tenant_scope` and `bytes`) that `MemoryRemember` writes in the same `BatchUpdate` as the record node, so neither exists without the other; one remember of a tenant runs at a time. The counter is exact on every path: `GraphTxn::add_node`, `GraphTxn::remove_node` and `compare_and_set_fields` move `memory-quota:<tenant>` by the stored bytes of any `memory:<tenant>:` node they write or remove, in the same transaction (so a hard delete, `forget`, evict, prune, a batch remove and a replayed removal all keep it exact), and admission never re-measures; a tenant with no counter node yet is measured once by a scan and the remember writes its counter. A projected total above the knob refuses `MEMORY_TENANT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (a `RefusalCode` of the `memory` table beside `MEMORY_ENTRY_TOO_LARGE`) with nothing written; the boundary is inclusive, so a total equal to the knob is admitted. The test `crates/medulla-h-graph/src/graph_ops/memory_surface_tests.rs::tenant_total_admission_keeps_a_durable_counter` covers the counter, the boundary, and delete-then-remember at the boundary, mark, delete and node-route removal. Eviction: a record becomes a prune candidate under the salience floor of R651.8. Knob `memory.entry_max_bytes` default 65536, [1024, 1048576], bytes, Fixed. Knob `memory.tenant_max_bytes` default 1073741824, [1048576, 1099511627776], bytes, Fixed. The registry exposes no per-corpus override. Writes: none. Depends: R651.1, R179.1. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R157.4` | **Delegation quality refusals.** Stage: 10 Learn, served operation `DecisionEval`. Refusals are registered in `delegation_quality::REFUSALS` (joined to the decision refusal registry through `codes::module_tables`; each code is also a `StatisticalErrorCode`). `DELEGATION_WINDOW_STALE` means `end_ms` is older than `knob delegation.window_max_age`. `DELEGATION_WINDOW_UNSTABLE` means the window is shorter than `knob delegation.min_window`. `DELEGATION_THRESHOLD_UNDEFINED` means a metric outside the closed `delegation_quality::METRICS` set (`task_success`, `review_accepted`, `defect_free`) or a value outside `[0, 1000000]`. `DELEGATION_INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLES` means the count is below `min_observations`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R158.2` | **Error-rate rule for model and width.** Stage: 6 Statistical rank. Code: `decide_adjustment(window: &ErrorWindow, current: &Current, tiers: &[ModelTier], knobs: &WidthKnobs) -> Result<ModelWidthAdjustment, AdjustmentRefusal>` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/run_adjustment.rs`. The error rate is `errored_runs / runs` in Q32. If the rate is at least `knob width.error_hi`, change two things. Choose the lowest legal model tier above the current one. Set width to `max(1, width - 1)`. If the rate is at most `knob width.error_lo`, keep the model and set width to `min(width + 1, host_ceiling)`. Otherwise change nothing. At the top tier the model stays. Knobs: `width.error_hi` 0.02, [0.01, 1.0], fraction. `width.error_lo` 0.005, [0, 0.5], fraction. `width.window` 20, [5, 200], runs. `width.min_runs` 10, [1, 200], runs. The host ceiling is the largest allowed width and is never exceeded. Fewer than `width.min_runs` runs abstains `INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLES`. Writes: none; `Decide` is evaluate-only (AD-4). Latency and cost inputs are added by R158.7. Caller chain: `Method::Decide` → `dispatch_decision_methods` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:112`) → `handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/statistical.rs:11`) → `stat_decide::handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:60`) → `serve` (`:79`) → `decide_blocking` (`:132`) → `family::for_kind` (R001.101, absent from the tree today) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/run_adjustment.rs` `conclude` → `decide_adjustment`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R160.2` | **Package validation behaviour.** Stage: 9 Commit, served operation `PublishSkillPackage`. Code: `pub fn validate_rendered_package(rendered: &RenderedSkillPackage, history: &[RunHistoryEntry]) -> Result<RenderedPackageValidation, PublicationRefusal>` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/package_validation.rs`. It is pure: it reads no clock, store or tenant policy. It returns the validation, not the receipt. The handler of R160.3 mints the `PublicationReceipt` from it, adding `package_id` and `publish_timestamp_ms` from its server clock parameter. **Inputs.** `rendered` is the `RenderedSkillPackage` the catalog projection rendered; its `digest` is parsed with `Digest256::parse`. `history` is the tenant-visible run history for that package, in recorded order; the handler reads it, so tenant scoping is the handler's job. **Knobs.** New `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/knob_families/package.rs` declares `KNOBS` with `package.min_runs` (default 1, range [1, 1000], unit runs, `Fixed`) and `package.min_pass_rate` (default 1000000, range [0, 1000000], unit micro-share, `Fixed`). It also declares `pub struct PackageKnobs { min_runs: u64, min_pass_rate_ppm: u64 }` and `pub fn knob_values() -> PackageKnobs`, which reads the two spec defaults. The table joins `knob_families::REGISTRY`. Both knobs are `Fixed`, so no tenant policy moves them, and the function stays two-argument. **Rule, in order; the first failing step refuses.** (1) `rendered.digest` does not parse refuses `DigestMismatch`. (2) Two entries with the same `run_id` refuse `RunSetInvalid`. (3) Fewer than `min_runs` entries refuse `RunHistoryMissing`. (4) An entry whose `package_digest` differs from the rendered digest refuses `DigestMismatch`. (5) `passed * 1000000 / len` below `min_pass_rate_ppm`, in integer arithmetic, refuses `ValidationFailed`. Otherwise it returns `RenderedPackageValidation { rendered_digest, run_history_digest: run_history_digest(history)?, validation_passed: true }`. A stored receipt therefore always carries `validation_passed: true`. **Refusal enum.** `PublicationRefusal`, defined once by R160.4, is the only error type; R160.2 adds no code. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R165.2` | **Necessity measure and comparison rule.** Stage: 6 Statistical rank. Code in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/tool_necessity.rs`: `measure_tool_necessity(runs: &[RunTraceRecord], tool_id, model_id, min_samples) -> Result<ToolNecessity, NecessityRefusal>` and `compare_tool_decision(necessity: &ToolNecessity, model_called: bool, necessary_min_q32: i64) -> ToolComparison`. Rule: keep runs of `model_id`. A run used the tool when a step has kind `tool_call` and `action_ref` equal to `tool_id`. Necessity is the success rate with the tool minus the success rate without it, as a Q32 difference. A run succeeded when its outcome is `succeeded`. The tool is necessary when necessity is at least `knob tool_necessity.necessary_min`. Agreement holds when necessary equals `model_called`. Knobs: `tool_necessity.min_samples` 30, [5, 1000], runs per arm. `tool_necessity.necessary_min` 0.1, [0, 1], fraction. `tool_necessity.window` 30 d, [1 d, 365 d], duration. `tool_necessity.max_age` 1 d, [1 h, 30 d], duration. Fewer samples in either arm abstains `INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLES`. Writes: none; `Decide` is evaluate-only (AD-4). Caller chain: `Method::Decide` → `dispatch_decision_methods` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:112`) → `handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/statistical.rs:11`) → `stat_decide::handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:60`) → `serve` (`:79`) → `decide_blocking` (`:132`) → `family::for_kind` (R001.101, absent from the tree today) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/tool_necessity.rs` `conclude` → `measure_tool_necessity` and `compare_tool_decision`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R167.2` | **Additive-only compatibility rule.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints, family `SkillUpgrade`, served operation `Decide`. Code: `fn compare_contracts(previous, new) -> ContractDiff` in `crates/medulla-decision-outcome-types/src/decision/skill_upgrade.rs`. Compatible means additive only. Every previous field must stay with the same `type_name` and must not turn from optional to required. Every field only in the new contract must be optional. Equal digests are compatible. A removed field, a type change or a new required field is breaking. `ContractDiff` lists `added_optional`, `added_required`, `removed`, `type_changed` and `became_required` field names (sorted); `is_compatible()` is true when the last four are empty. Equal contracts have an empty diff. A required field that becomes optional stays compatible. A breaking upgrade needs a declared migration id. This rule is a safety check and has no knob. Caller chain: `Method::Decide` → `dispatch_decision_methods` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:112`) → `handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/statistical.rs:11`) → `stat_decide::handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:60`) → `serve` (`:79`) → `decide_blocking` (`:132`) → `family::for_kind` (R001.101, absent from the tree today) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/skill_upgrade.rs` `conclude` → `compare_contracts`. Shape: `compare_contracts` is a pure function added to the existing `crates/medulla-decision-outcome-types/src/decision/skill_upgrade.rs`; the digest is SHA-256 over canonical bytes with fields sorted by name. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R172.4` | **Rank blend.** Stage: 6 Statistical rank, served by `Decide`. Add `rank_capability_candidates(pool, question, rewards, policy)` in `crates/medulla-decision-rank/src/rank/capability_rank.rs`. L2-normalize stored and query vectors; similarity is the inner product. Take the best `min(pool_size, max(k, oversample_factor * k))` by cosine. Score = cosine + `reward_weight` * (reward - 0.5) + `prior_weight` * (prior - 0.5). The weights come from the question's `weights`; the knobs below are the ceilings a question's weight is clamped to. Knob `designation.reward_weight` default 0.15, range [0, 1], unit weight. Knob `designation.prior_weight` default 0.15, range [0, 1], unit weight. All knobs are `Tunable`. The default prior applies when the question gives no prior and records carry an ontology type. The modal type of the oversampled pool gets 1.0. Other types get 0.5. With no stored types the prior term is off. A weight of zero turns its term off; with both off the order is pure cosine. Ties order by entity id ascending. Return at most k designations, each with its swappable alternatives sorted by id. Caller chain: `Method::Decide` → `dispatch_decision_methods` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:112`) → `handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/statistical.rs:11`) → `stat_decide::handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:60`) → `serve` (`:79`) → `decide_blocking` (`:132`) → `family::for_kind` (R001.101, absent from the tree today) → `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/capability_designation.rs` `conclude` → `rank_capability_candidates`. Shape: New `crates/medulla-decision-rank/src/rank/capability_rank.rs` in the scaffold crate `medulla-decision-rank` (level L4, below `medulla-decision-memory` L6, which calls it); declare `pub mod rank;` in its `lib.rs`; takes the oversampled pool by value, so it needs no index type; knobs from the knob table of R179. Verified by the root slice test `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/capability_designation_tests.rs::designation_journey`. Planned: see `test-spec.md`, heading Planned bindings, range 5. |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R172.5` | **Reward update rule.** Stage: 10 Learn, served by `DecisionLog` (op `capability_outcome`). Add `apply_capability_outcome(reward, outcome, revision, policy)` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/capability_designation.rs`. The outcome is `success: bool` (1 or 0) or an explicit reward clamped to [0, 1]. The update is an exponential moving average, `new = (1 - alpha) * old + alpha * observed`, with neutral start 0.5. Knob `designation.reward_alpha` default 0.3, range [0.01, 1], unit weight. All arithmetic is Q32 fixed point, so replay is deterministic (R007). `generation_erasure` applies when a writer upserts a record again with a changed vector. If the cosine distance to the stored vector is above `knob designation.reembed_reset_distance`, reset the reward to 0.5 and increment `generation`. That knob has default 0.25, range [0.05, 1], unit cosine distance. `selective_erase(ids)` resets only the named ids and is order-independent. `decay(factor)` applies `0.5 + (r - 0.5) * factor` with knob `designation.reward_decay` default 0.99, range [0.5, 1]. Persistence is `.5.1`. Caller chain: `Method::DecisionLog` → `dispatch_decision_methods` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:133`) → `handle_decision_log` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/log.rs:11`) → `stat_log::handle_log` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_log.rs:541`) → `apply_capability_outcome` (this row) for op `capability_outcome` (R172.7.1). | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R175.2` | **Behavior: residual quantization and refinement.** Stage: 5 rank; served operation `Decide` (kind `item_recommendation`). Add `fit_codebooks`, `encode_item` and `refine_and_rank` in new `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/recommend.rs`. Fitting uses seeded k-means per level. The seed is the first 8 bytes of `catalog_digest`. Each pause step moves the working vector `v` by `v = v + knob recommend.pause_alpha * (mean_history - v)`. It then pulls `v` toward the nearest item by `knob recommend.nearest_pull`. Ranking filters to the code-prefix bucket of the refined vector, then orders by cosine on the Q32 scale. When the bucket holds fewer than `top_k` items, the bucket drops its last level. Encode cost is O(L*C*d) per item. Query cost is O(p*(h+m)*d) plus the bucket size. Knob `recommend.levels` default 4, [1, 4], levels. Knob `recommend.codes_per_level` default 256, [2, 256], codes. Knob `recommend.kmeans_iters` default 20, [1, 100], iterations. Knob `recommend.pause_alpha` default 0.5, [0, 1], unitless. Knob `recommend.nearest_pull` default 0.25, [0, 1], unitless. Writes: none. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R173.7` | **The engine moves `core:editStatus`: `HarnessEdit` serves the edit lifecycle through `EditMachine`.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints, state ownership (organization constitution Article XXXI); served operation `HarnessEdit` (new `Method` variant). Decision: the engine owns the transitions of a harness edit's `core:editStatus`; a caller asks for an event and the engine decides. **Machine.** `EditMachine` in new file `crates/medulla-types/src/edit_machine.rs`. States: closed enum `EditStatus` (`Proposed`, `Shipped`, `Reverted`; stored forms `proposed`, `shipped`, `reverted`; the enum moves here from `crates/medulla-decision-outcome-types/src/decision/concentration.rs`, which re-exports it). Initial state `Proposed`; terminal state `Reverted`. Events: closed enum `EditEvent` (`Ship`, `Revert`). Edges: `E01` `Proposed` `Ship` `Shipped`; `E02` `Proposed` `Revert` `Reverted`; `E03` `Shipped` `Revert` `Reverted`. Every other pair is refused. Transition function: `EditStatus::apply(event) -> Result<EditStatus, TransitionRefused>`, the only code that computes a next status. Refusal: `TransitionRefused` of MEDULLA-ORCH-VOCAB-R811.4 with machine `EditMachine`, wire code `TRANSITION_REFUSED`; `HarnessEdit` joins `MACHINE_METHODS`. Ontology: `:EditMachine` of `:StateMachine` in `crates/medulla-core/ontology/state-machines-v1.ttl`, one state per variant with its `:storedForm`, one transition per edge with `:fromState`, `:toState` and `:firedBy`, classes extending the core state-machine classes by `rdfs:subClassOf`, no `owl:imports`. **Served method.** `Method::HarnessEdit { op: Box<HarnessEditOp> }` in `crates/medulla-protocol-types/src/protocol/method/method_11.rs`; `HarnessEditOp` in new file `crates/medulla-work-types/src/harness_edit.rs` has two ops: `Transition { edit_id, event }`, the only mutation, and `Get { edit_id }`, a graph read. Both answer `HarnessEditRecord { edit_id, status }`. The request carries no tenant: the tenant is the verified request tenant, and the graph is the request graph. The edit is the node `edit_id` of that graph that carries `_harness_edit: true`. A node that is absent, is not a harness edit, or carries a `tenant_id` other than the verified tenant answers the one non-disclosing refusal `HARNESS_EDIT_UNKNOWN`. A stored `editStatus` that is not one of the three stored forms (including the retired word `rejected`) refuses `HARNESS_EDIT_STATUS_INVALID`; the engine never repairs it. Both codes are the `REFUSALS` of `harness_edit.rs`, registered in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/codes.rs` `module_tables` and listed for `HarnessEdit` in `EXACT_METHOD_ERRORS`, with `PARAMETER_INVALID` (an empty `edit_id`) and `REVISION_CONFLICT`. **Write.** `Transition` is gateway-routed (`Route::HarnessEdit` in `crates/medulla-h-graph/src/graph_ops/gateway_graph_routes.rs`): the handler `crates/medulla-h-graph/src/graph_ops/harness_edit.rs` reads the node, applies the event with `EditStatus::apply`, and commits one `AddNode` upsert of the same properties with only `editStatus` replaced. The commit closure re-reads `editStatus` and refuses `REVISION_CONFLICT` when it is no longer the status the event was applied to, so two racing events never both apply. A refused transition writes nothing. The scope is `harness:edit`, local-only authority like `ObservationState`. **Reads of the status.** `stat_concentration.rs` keeps reading the literal; it is now always a word this machine wrote, except for nodes written before this row, which the engine neither migrates nor reinterprets. Not covered: a direct graph write that sets the literal bypasses the machine; closing that needs a graph-write guard, which is a separate row. Python: the wire models `HarnessEditOp`, `EditEvent` and `MethodHarnessEdit` in `medulla/generated/models.py`, the sender `send_harness_edit` in `medulla/generated/coordination.py` and `DecisionClient.harness_edit` in `medulla/decision_client.py`, maintained by hand with the Rust change. Registries: the method policy (`crates/medulla-capabilities/src/domains/coordination.rs`), scope `harness:edit`, `EXACT_METHOD_ERRORS`, `MACHINE_METHODS`, the result contract, write classification, the gateway plan, the CDC marker and the audit line, each with the entries of `ObservationState`. Caller chain: `Method::HarnessEdit` -> `dispatch_graph_op` gateway route `Route::HarnessEdit` -> `harness_edit::handle_transition` -> `EditStatus::apply` -> `commit_gateway_coalescable`; the get is `try_handle_harness_edit` in the graph read path. Writes: the one node upsert. Depends: R173.3, R830.4. | Test: `crates/medulla-types/src/edit_machine.rs::tests::every_legal_transition_applies`, `crates/medulla-types/src/edit_machine.rs::tests::every_illegal_pair_is_refused_with_transition_refused`, `crates/medulla-types/src/edit_machine.rs::tests::no_writer_sets_status_outside_apply` and `crates/medulla-rdf/tests/state_machine_vocabulary.rs::edit_machine_matches_edge_table` (L1). `crates/medulla-h-graph/src/graph_ops/harness_edit_tests.rs::transitions_move_the_status_and_refuse_illegal_pairs` and `crates/medulla-h-graph/src/graph_ops/harness_edit_tests.rs::foreign_tenant_edit_reads_as_unknown` (L3). |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R173.8` | **Only `HarnessEdit` sets `editStatus`: the mutation compiler refuses every caller write of it, and `HarnessEdit` gains the create op.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints, state ownership (organization constitution Article XXXI). R173.7 makes `HarnessEdit` the one served mover of a harness edit's `editStatus`; this row closes the generic write route, creation included. On origin/main no production code outside `crates/medulla-h-graph/src/graph_ops/harness_edit.rs` writes `editStatus` (`git grep editStatus` over `crates/`, `src/`, `medulla/` and `scripts/` finds only that writer, its reader in `stat_concentration.rs`, the ontology and shapes, and tests); edits are created today by callers through generic node writes, and that route moves to the create op below. **Create op.** `HarnessEditOp` (`crates/medulla-work-types/src/harness_edit.rs:36`) gains `Create { edit_id: String, dimension_iri: String, round: u32, policy_revision: Option<u64> }`; `is_mutation` is true for `Create` and `Transition`; `check` refuses an empty `edit_id` or `dimension_iri` with `PARAMETER_INVALID`. `handle_transition` (renamed `handle_mutation`) serves it: when node `edit_id` already exists in the request graph it refuses the new code `HARNESS_EDIT_EXISTS` (added to the `REFUSALS` of `harness_edit.rs` and to the `HarnessEdit` entry of `EXACT_METHOD_ERRORS`) and writes nothing; otherwise it commits ONE `Method::BatchUpdate` (an `upsert_node` plus an `upsert_edge`) through `commit_gateway` (a non-coalescable staged diff: a coalescable commit takes one `Method` and its prepublish fast path derives the durable row from that method alone, so an edge written inside the apply closure would not be durable), refusing `PARAMETER_INVALID` first when `dimension_iri` is not an existing node (an edge needs both endpoints); the node properties are `{"_harness_edit": true, "editStatus": "proposed", "editRound": round, "tenant_id": <verified tenant>}` plus `"policyRevision": policy_revision` when present, and the edge `edit_id` to `dimension_iri` with properties `{"relationship": "targetsDimension"}`, the node and edge shape `stat_concentration.rs` reads. The answer is `HarnessEditRecord { edit_id, status: EditStatus::Proposed }`. The initial state `Proposed` comes from `EditMachine`, never from the caller. **Chokepoint.** `compile_methods_with_outbox` (`crates/medulla-server-api/src/batch_compile/compile.rs:140`), where typed principal metadata is already admitted for every node-writing route (MEDULLA-IDENTITY-R023.9/R023.10), and `compile_crossmodal` (`compile.rs:391`), the transaction compiler; both call the guard before any operation is compiled. **Guard.** New `pub fn refuse_direct_edit_status(method: &Method) -> Result<(), String>` in new `crates/medulla-server-api/src/mutation_batch/edit_status.rs` (declared in `crates/medulla-server-api/src/mutation_batch.rs`). It reuses the private `properties_of` and `statement_text` of `crates/medulla-server-api/src/mutation_batch/identity_metadata.rs`, made `pub(crate)`. The guard also covers `CompareAndSetNodeFields.updates_msgpack`, the create, CAS and claim operations of `Method::Batch`, and every depth of a `BatchUpdate` document, so no generic route sets the status; `compile_crossmodal` sees only a manifest digest, so for it the guard runs in `h-txn::compile_cross_modal_batch` over `args.methods` before it is called. `properties_of` takes `&mut`, so a read-only `properties_blob` is added beside it in `identity_metadata.rs`. A node write (`AddNode`, `CreateNodeIfAbsent`, `TxnAddNode` and every method `properties_of` reads) whose decoded properties hold the key `editStatus`, with any value including `proposed`, is refused. A statement method (`Sql`, `CypherQuery`, `ApplyMutation`, RDF writes, every method `statement_text` reads) whose text names `editStatus` is refused. No value is exempt, so nothing outside `HarnessEdit` can create, overwrite or move the status, and no graph read is needed. **Refusal.** New `EDIT_STATUS_ENGINE_OWNED: RefusalCode` in `crates/medulla-types/src/edit_machine.rs`, message `EDIT_STATUS_ENGINE_OWNED: editStatus is written only through HarnessEdit`. It is not `TRANSITION_REFUSED`, because the refused methods move no machine and `MACHINE_METHODS` (`crates/medulla-capabilities/src/error_routing.rs:1708`) must not list them. Register it in `method_error_set` next to the R023.10 node-writing list (`error_routing.rs`, the `matches!` that inserts `CORRUPT_MUTATION_LEDGER`), for `AddNode`, `CreateNodeIfAbsent`, `TxnAddNode`, `ApplyMutation`, `Sql`, `CypherQuery`, `AddTriples` and the four `ApplyChangeEnvelope*` methods. **How `HarnessEdit` is told apart.** On main the transition commits a synthetic `Method::AddNode` through `commit_gateway_coalescable`, and nothing that reaches the compiler distinguishes it from a caller's `AddNode`. So the writer is explicit: new `Copy` enum `StatusWriter { Caller, EditMachine, Replicated }` in `crates/medulla-types/src/edit_machine.rs`. `CompileBatch` (`compile.rs:95`) and `MutationCtx` (`crates/medulla-server-mutation/src/mutation/context.rs:17`) gain `pub status_writer: StatusWriter`. `compile_batch_context` (`crates/medulla-server-mutation/src/mutation/commit_replay.rs:35`) copies it from the `MutationCtx`. Every existing constructor sets `Caller`. `handle_mutation` commits both `Create` and `Transition` with `MutationCtx { status_writer: StatusWriter::EditMachine, ..*ctx }`. The raft re-compilation sites (`crates/medulla-raft/src/raft/mod.rs:590`, `crates/medulla-raft/src/raft/store.rs:315`, `crates/medulla-raft/src/raft/store/commit.rs:74`, `crates/medulla-raft/src/raft/store/replay.rs:120` and `:338`) set `Replicated`, because the leader already admitted the batch. The guard runs only for `Caller`. **Callers and tests.** Every test fixture and served test that seeds a harness edit with a generic write (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/concentration_tests.rs`, `tests/decide/test_concentration_served.py` of R173.6) seeds through `HarnessEdit` `Create`, or writes the graph core directly below the compiler in unit tests. Python: `HarnessEditOp` in `medulla/generated/models.py` gains the `create` variant, maintained by hand with the Rust change. Writes: the create node and edge, through `HarnessEdit` only; a refused write commits nothing. Caller chain: served `AddNode` -> `try_handle_gateway` (`crates/medulla-h-graph/src/graph_ops/gateway.rs:57`) -> `commit_gateway_coalescable` -> `commit_coalescable_mutation` -> `compile_batch_context` -> `compile_methods_with_outbox` -> `refuse_direct_edit_status`; `Method::HarnessEdit` `Create` or `Transition` -> gateway route `Route::HarnessEdit` -> `harness_edit::handle_mutation` -> the same chain with `StatusWriter::EditMachine`. Shape: one new file in `medulla-server-api`; one enum and one code in `edit_machine.rs`; one op and one code in `harness_edit.rs`; one field on `CompileBatch` and `MutationCtx`; one error-routing entry. Depends: MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R173.7. | Test: `crates/medulla-server-api/src/mutation_batch/edit_status.rs::tests::caller_writes_of_edit_status_are_refused` (L1) asserts that a caller `AddNode` with `editStatus` `proposed`, one with `shipped`, and a `Sql` text naming `editStatus` each refuse `EDIT_STATUS_ENGINE_OWNED`, and that the same `AddNode` compiled under `StatusWriter::EditMachine` or `Replicated` passes. Served L3 tests in `crates/medulla-server-served-tests` (`harness_edit_served_tests.rs`): `harness_edit_create_is_served` (a served `HarnessEdit` `Create` writes the `proposed` node and its edge), `second_create_refuses_harness_edit_exists` and `served_add_node_of_edit_status_is_refused`. `crates/medulla-h-graph/src/graph_ops/harness_edit_tests.rs::only_harness_edit_sets_edit_status` (L3, compile-level: h-graph has no served dispatch harness) asserts that a served caller `AddNode` with `editStatus` `proposed` is refused and writes no node, that `HarnessEdit` `Create` writes the edit as `proposed` with its `targetsDimension` edge, that a second `Create` refuses `HARNESS_EDIT_EXISTS`, that a caller `AddNode` setting `shipped` on it is refused and leaves `proposed`, and that `HarnessEdit` `Transition` `Ship` then answers `shipped`. |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R134.110.2` | **Behavior: lexical and embedding fusion.** Stage: 6 Statistical rank. Served operation `Decide` with `QuestionKind::ToolRelevance`. Code: `fuse_tool_ranks` in `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/tool_relevance.rs`, next to `rank_tools_by_relevance` (R134.2). It reuses `bm25::scores` and adds no second inverted index. Rule: filter tools by the role allowlist first. The allowlist is the `toolset_refs` of the published `Toolset` component whose id equals `agent_role_iri`. An empty `agent_role_iri` applies no allowlist. Lexical arm: candidate-local `bm25::scores` over `name` and `description` of the allowed visible tools. An invisible tool never moves a score. Embedding arm, used when `task_embedding` is present: cosine similarity between the Q32 task embedding and each stored tool embedding. Use integer dot products and an IEEE square root. Quantise once with `quant::q32`. Fuse by reciprocal rank: `fused = sum over arms of 1 / (knob tool_relevance.rrf_k + rank)` with `rrf_k` defaulting to 60 ([1, 1000], rank units), ranks counted from 1. `relevance = fused / (arms * 1 / (rrf_k + 1))`, a Q32 value in [0, 1]. Ties order by tool id. Refusals: `EMBEDDING_DIMENSION_MISMATCH` when the task and tool embedding lengths differ. Evidence: R134.110.5. Writes: none. The run receipt key is `run_credit/run/<run_id>`, written with `store_once`. `Discover` hit rows and `arm_ranks` are the returned rows that `record_run` credits. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R174.8.4` | **Refusal and the write that executes a refresh plan.** Stage: 10 learn; served operation `DecisionLog` (`Learn`). Drift policy: one `DriftPolicyNode { schema_version, logical_graph, region_budget }` per tenant and logical graph (new, in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/retrieval_drift.rs`; `region_budget` is a `u32` in [1, 4096], so it can only lower the 4,096-region cap of `RefreshPlan`). It is stored as the decision artifact `drift-policy:<logical_graph>` by the new write `LearningWrite::RegisterDriftPolicy { logical_graph, region_budget }`, which replaces the previous node of that graph (a keyed `put_decision_artifacts`, not `store_once`) and answers `LearningRecorded::DriftPolicy(Box<DriftPolicyNode>)`. Evaluation: `EvaluateDrift` (`stat_learning.rs:163`, `evaluate_drift`) gains `priority: RefreshPriority` (`#[serde(default)]`, default `downtime`). It first reads the policy and answers `DRIFT_POLICY_MISSING` when the graph has none (before any plan is stored), and a plan whose region count exceeds the policy's `region_budget` (counted before `RefreshPlan::new`, which only knows the 4,096 cap) answers `REFRESH_REGION_BUDGET`. Execution: the new write `LearningWrite::RefreshDrift { logical_graph, plan_digest, capacity_cell }` is the only executor of a plan; `RunGenerationCycle` is unchanged and is not used. `prepare` loads the `ScheduledRefresh` stored as `drift-plan:<plan_digest>` (absent or another tenant's reads as absent and refuses `PARAMETER_INVALID`), resolves the logical graph as a materialized graph (`graphs_of` returns it for this write) and acquires the analytics lease with `acquire_drift_lease` (the `drift-eval` job id is replaced by `drift-refresh:<plan_digest>`). `dispatch` then (a) returns the recorded receipt when the node `drift-refresh:<plan_digest>` exists, embedding and swapping nothing; (b) checks every shard of the plan against `ScheduledRefresh.shard_generations` through `DriftRegistry::verify_generations` before any embedding; (c) re-embeds each distinct node of the graph whose `type` property equals the `node_type` of a plan region, in batches of `knobs().generation_batch_nodes`, with the prepared `Reembedder` (`ConfiguredEmbedder`) and `GraphVectors::store_embedding` exactly as `reembed_batch` (`stat_generation_cycle.rs:222`) does; (d) plans the swap with `DriftRegistry::planned_swaps(tenant, graph, expected: &[(u32, u64)], durable: &BTreeMap<u32, u64>) -> Result<Vec<(u32, u64, u64)>, SwapConflict>` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/drift_registry.rs`), which verifies and changes nothing, and builds the receipt. The receipt is a graph node `drift-refresh:<plan_digest>` of type `DriftRefreshReceipt` (the `DriftRefreshed` fields), staged in the same batch as the shard pointer nodes, so neither exists without the other and a failed commit leaves no receipt; a replay reads the recorded receipt from that node. Durable first: the served write commits the pointer nodes (`commit_refresh_link`), and only after that commit succeeded does it apply the in-memory swap with `DriftRegistry::apply_committed_swaps` and feed the re-embedded vectors to the monitors through the `DiscoverSignals::observe_write` port (the `RefreshApply` closure the write staged); a failed commit applies nothing, so memory is never ahead of the store. The generation pointer is durable: one graph node per shard, `drift-shard:<logical_graph>/<shard>` of type `DriftShardGeneration` (`ShardGenerationNode { schema_version, logical_graph, shard_id, generation }`), staged by the swap and committed through the durable mutation path (`commit_refresh_link`) before the answer returns. A shard's current generation is its pointer node when it has one, else its monitor's, else the plan's own (a restart emptied the registry and no swap ever ran, so nothing moved it); `planned_swaps` takes the registry lock once and verifies for every `(shard, generation)` that the current generation is the expected one and that a present monitor is `Monitoring`; `apply_committed_swaps`, run only after the pointer commit, applies `ShardMonitorEvent::Refresh` to each present monitor and sets the committed generation (a new edge S04 of `SHARD_MONITOR_MACHINE` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/shard_monitor.rs`: `Monitoring` to `Warming`, fresh reference moments and vocabulary filter, `generation` + 1; the first seal makes generation 1 and a re-seal adds no second increment). It returns `(shard, before, after)` per shard. A mismatch changes nothing and surfaces as `SHARD_SWAP_CONFLICT`. Because the pointer is durable, a restart never produces `SHARD_SWAP_CONFLICT` for a plan that no other swap has moved. Graph materialization (decided: a refresh writes the refreshed row into the tenant graph as well as the decision artifact; `Discover` has no special path): for every `New` or `Superseded` result, `refresh_with` also builds one graph batch for the request's graph, when it is a registered tenant graph with Write access (a virtual-only graph keeps artifacts only), applied by `stat_log::commit_refresh_link` after the artifacts are stored through `commit_internal_graph_methods_with_nonce` (the `RunRecord` link path): `upsert_node` with id `freshness:<sha256(graph, canonical url)>`, node type `Document`, properties `name` (title), `description` (snippet), `url`, `content_digest`, `provenance` `{source, fetched_at, receipt, query_digest}`, `source` (the `source_connection_iri`), `fetched_at` (the `retrieved_at` of the `FreshResult`, epoch milliseconds), `receipt` (the `refresh_id`) and `supersedes` (the previous digest, when superseded), and an `AddEmbedding` of the bound text embedder's vector of `title`, a newline and `snippet` (the configured embedder, with the space check of `run_record`; with no embedder bound the refresh refuses `QUERY_ENCODER_UNAVAILABLE` before any write). A retry after a failed graph commit finds the row held (`Unchanged`); the row text for that case: the refresh writes the node for an `Unchanged` result whose node is absent, so a retry repairs the graph. The L4 asserts Discover (keyword) returns the row and its provenance; the drift re-embed is asserted by the L3 plan test only (it needs a capacity lease). A repeated id upserts the same node, so a superseded row replaces its predecessor. `Discover` then returns the row like any node of the graph, with `source`, `fetched_at` and `receipt` as its provenance. The drift loader needs no new call: the `AddEmbedding` commit is a vector write that `DriftRegistry::observe_write` (`drift_registry.rs`, installed by `drift_registry::install`) already sees, so the region of the refreshed row is marked by the ordinary write path and the next `evaluate_drift` for that shard re-embeds it; the `RegionMark`s in the `FreshnessReceipt` are the evidence of which shard each row fell in. The Python `LearningRecorded` union and its members (`refreshed`, `monitored`, `calibration`, `cycle`, `drift`, `feedback`, `package_run`, `distilled_scores`, with `FreshnessReceipt`, `FreshResult` and `RegionMark`) are mirrored in `medulla/generated/models.py` in the same commit that lands the L4 below, because it decodes them. L4 steps: register `search` through `RegisterForeignSource` with the loopback `WebGateway`; send `DecisionLog` `Learn` `Refresh` twice (the second reports `unchanged_count` equal to the first's `new_count`); change one recorded result's snippet in the gateway fixture and refresh again (`superseded_count` 1); `Discover` with the changed snippet's words returns the `freshness:` node with `source`, `fetched_at` and `receipt`; the drift evaluation of that shard lists the region. Nightly group `decide/retrieval_learning` (R178.1) holds the budget of 2 ms p99 engine overhead per 100 results, excluding connector latency. Writes: `DecisionLog` writes the refresh. Caller chain: `Method::DecisionLog` arm (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:133`) → `handle_decision_log` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/log.rs:11`) → `handle_log` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_log.rs:541`) → `dispatch` (`stat_log.rs:459`) → `stat_learning::dispatch` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_learning.rs:163`). Shape: no production file (a served test over the rows it proves); reuse the served-test kit. Depends: R174.9.3.1, R174.9.4, R174.9.5. | Tests: `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/freshness_refresh_tests.rs::search_refresh_dedupes_and_feeds_drift_refresh` (L3) covers the journey. `tests/decide/test_freshness_refresh_served.py::test_search_refresh_dedupes_and_feeds_refresh` (L4) runs it through the client. |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R614.2.5` | **Fit topic centroids from labelled examples.** Stage: 10 Learn, served by `SemanticEnrich`. Add `fit_topics(examples: &[LabelledVector], holdout_bp: u16) -> Result<FittedTopics, EnrichError>` in `crates/medulla-enrich/src/semantic.rs`, beside `classify` (`:353`). `LabelledVector` holds a topic id, a vector and an example id. The centroid of a topic is the mean of its training vectors, scaled to unit length. A seeded split sets aside `holdout_bp` basis points of each topic (default 2000, range 0 to 5000; any other value refuses `KNOB_OUT_OF_BOUNDS`). The split orders a topic's examples by the digest of the fixed seed `eg/fit-topics/v1` and the example id, so it depends on the example ids alone, and sets aside the first `ceil(n * holdout_bp / 10000)` of them, never all of them. Each hold-out example is classified against every fitted centroid with a floor of zero; the precision of a topic is the share of the hold-out examples assigned to it that belong to it (0 when none is assigned). The fit must report, per topic, the hold-out precision and a confidence floor. The floor is the lowest `classify` confidence that reaches 90 percent precision on the hold-out, or 10000 when none does. Each topic needs at least 5 examples. Refusals: `TOPIC_EXAMPLES_TOO_FEW`, `VECTOR_DIMENSION_MISMATCH`. The fit is pure and writes nothing, and it returns `FittedTopics { holdout_bp, topics }` with one `FittedTopic { topic, centroid, holdout_precision_bp, floor_bp, train_examples, holdout_examples }` per topic in topic id order. `TopicCentroid` gains `floor_bp: Option<u32>`; `classify_with_floor` uses the winning topic's stored floor in place of the fixed cut when it has one. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R750.751` | **Behaviour.** Stage: 6 Statistical rank, served by `Decide`. Code: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/thought_search.rs`, function `choose_expansion(state,strategy,knobs)`. Stop when `nodes_used` reaches `max_nodes`, `tokens_used` reaches `max_tokens`, or no leaf is below `max_depth`. Otherwise expand `n` leaves, where `n` is the strategy width limited by the remaining node budget divided by `max_branching`. If `n` is 0, stop. `Chain` expands the single leaf with the highest score. `Tree` expands up to `beam_width` leaves of the least depth, by score descending. `Planning` expands up to `beam_width` leaves by score descending over all depths. `Graph` first merges leaves with equal `state_digest` into the lowest id, keeps the highest score, then acts as `Tree`. Ties order by id ascending. The best node is the one with the highest score, ties by id. `path_digest` is the SHA-256 of the root-to-best node ids and scores. A budget stop sets `certified_gap`. It sets `gap` to the highest unexpanded score minus the best score, floored at 0. Writes: none. Caller chain: `Method::Decide` arm (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:112`) → `handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:60`) → `serve` (`stat_decide.rs:79`) → `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/thought_search.rs` (`choose_expansion`). Shape: files `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/thought_search.rs`; nearest existing sibling `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/adapter.rs`; reuse a pure, deterministic function with no I/O, following `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/exploration.rs` for knob-bounded behaviour and `aggregate_log` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_log.rs:302`) for outcome rates. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R751.751` | **Behaviour (reward kernels).** Stage: 6 Statistical rank, served by `Decide`. Code: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/reward.rs`, function `decompose(request,knobs)`. Progress of step `i` is `value_estimate[i]` minus `value_estimate[i-1]`, with the first predecessor 0. The weight is `max(progress, knob reward.difficulty_floor)` (default 0.01, [0.001, 1], ratio) times `1 - knob reward.cache_tier_discount` (default 0.5, [0, 1], ratio) when `cache_hit` is true. The step reward is `floor(trajectory_reward * weight / total_weight)`. The last step takes the rounding remainder. The rewards then sum exactly to the trajectory reward. The normalised advantage is `(reward - mean) / std`, computed in Q32 with an integer square root. `keep_for_training` is true when the trajectory reward lies strictly inside two bounds. The low bound is `knob reward.saturation_low` (default 0, [0, 1], ratio). The high bound is `knob reward.saturation_high` (default 1, [0, 1], ratio). A node reward is the sum of the step rewards in its range. The function is deterministic, and repeated calls for one trajectory id return identical bytes. When `proposed_rewards` is present, the function verifies it instead. The sum must lie within `knob reward.sum_tolerance` of the trajectory reward (default 0.000001, [0, 0.001], ratio). Writes: none. Caller chain: `Method::Decide` arm (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:112`) → `handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:60`) → `serve` (`stat_decide.rs:79`) → `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/reward.rs` (`decompose`). Depends: R751.750. Implementation: `decompose(request, &RewardKnobs)` with `RewardKnobs::from_policy` and the five `reward.*` knobs declared in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/reward.rs` and registered in `knob_families::REGISTRY`; ratio knobs are `DecimalMicros` and become `Q32` through `numeric::micros_to_q32` (round half up). A step weight is `max(progress, floor)`, times `1 - discount` for a cache hit; the reward is `floor(R * weight / total)` and the last step takes the remainder. When the discount zeroes every weight the request is refused. A hierarchy node must name steps inside the trace and an earlier parent; a bad node is refused. | Tests: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/reward.rs::tests::rewards_sum_exactly_and_floor_applies` (L1), `tests::cache_hit_discounts_weight` (L1) and `tests::decomposition_is_idempotent` (L2, golden vector). Code: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/population.rs`, functions `wasserstein1(reference,current)` and `fanout_width(spread,current_width,budget,knobs)`. Both windows sort ascending. With `m` the larger window length, quantile `k` of a window of length `n` is element `floor((2k+1)*n/(2m))`. The distance is the mean absolute quantile difference over `k` from 0 to `m-1`, rounded half up on scale Q32. The reading alerts when the distance exceeds `knob drift.alert` (default 0.10, [0, 1], ratio). The mean diversity `D` is the mean of the pairwise entries. The width rises by 1 when `D` reaches `knob fanout.diversity_high` (default 0.40, [0, 1], ratio). It falls by 1, to a minimum of 1, when `D` is at most `knob fanout.diversity_low` (default 0.15, [0, 1], ratio). Otherwise it stays. The cap is the lesser of `knob fanout.replica_ceiling` (default 8, [1, 64], replicas) and `floor(budget / cost_per_replica)`. The width never exceeds the cap. All arithmetic is fixed-point integer. Code: `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/trajectory_join.rs`, function `join(entries)`, and `step_verify.rs`, functions `verify_steps(request,knobs)` and `admit(probes,knobs)`. A join keeps the entry with the strongest evidence (`Proof`, then `Observation`, then `Claim`). Ties break on the higher verifier score, then on the lexicographically smallest trajectory id. Distillation returns every source id sorted, the winner id and `derivation_digest`. The digest is the SHA-256 of the sorted source ids joined by newlines. A verifier recomputes the SHA-256 of the step digests in order and binds the verdict to it. The first failed step selects the recovery. It is `Retry` while attempts are below `knob verify.max_retries` (default 2, [0, 5], attempts). Otherwise it is `Rollback` to the last passed step, or `Abandon` when none passed. Admission requires between 1 and `knob verify.probe_budget` probes (default 8, [1, 64], probes). It allows no `Compromised` verdict. It allows at most `knob verify.max_inconclusive` inconclusive verdicts (`Fixed`, 0, count). Writes: none. Depends: R753.750. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R650.5` | **Descriptor evidence.** Stage: 8 Record. The sealed record lists premises with these exact meanings: `descriptor_version:<id>=<n>` where `<id>` is the capability id (the option id) and `<n>` is `descriptor.version` (decimal `u64`), one per designated capability; `ontology_digest:<digest>` where `<digest>` is the lowercase hex digest of the closure ontology the closure was projected from; `closure_member:<iri>` one per member of the closure, in ascending byte order of the IRI; `reward_revision:<entity>=<n>` where `<entity>` is the capability id and `<n>` is the `record_revision` of the reward entry that scored it, present only for a capability that has one. The weakest evidence class is `Observation`. A designation outcome is an `Advisory`, and an advisory is evaluate-only and never logged (`stat_replay.rs::loggable` admits only `Acted`, `Explored` and `Abstained`; this row changes no log rule), so the evidence is read from the sealed record that the `Decide` response returns, never through `DecisionLog` `Get`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R651.4` | **Refusal.** Stage: 0 admit; operation `MemoryRemember`, and the hard-removal routes `EvictBelow` and `Maintain` with `delete = true`. Register the two codes below as `RefusalCode` constants in `crates/medulla-work-types/src/memory.rs` and add them to its `REFUSALS` table (R010.100), and as `ServerErrorCode` variants routed for `MemoryRemember`, `EvictBelow` and `Maintain`. (1) A `MemoryRemember` whose `record.tenant` differs from the verified tenant answers exactly like a record that does not exist for the caller: `PARAMETER_INVALID` with the message `memory record <id> does not exist`, byte for byte the answer for a record that does not exist (`memory_surface::absent_record` is the one producer), never `ACCESS_DENIED`, never a tenant-specific code, and a message that never mentions a tenant, so the answer confirms nothing about another tenant's records. A foreign tenant's stored record reads as absent to `MemoryRecall`, `MemoryExport` and `MemoryRead` (already true, unchanged). The L3 assertion at `memory_surface_tests.rs:102` changes to `refusal.starts_with("PARAMETER_INVALID")` and asserts neither `ACCESS_DENIED` nor a tenant code, that the refusal equals `absent_record(<id>)` exactly and that its text contains no tenant word, with the `core.node_count() == 0` assertion kept. (2) `MEMORY_ENTRY_TOO_LARGE` refuses a record whose stored encoding is above `knob memory.entry_max_bytes` (registered in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/knob_families/memory.rs`; default 65536, range [1024, 1048576], bytes). The size is `node_blob(tenant, request)?.len()` in `memory_surface.rs`, the msgpack property map that is written as the node (the record's properties plus the tenant key), so the measure is exactly the bytes the node would store, not the text length and not the wire JSON. The check runs in `admit_remember` after the `PARAMETER_INVALID` checks and before the embedding and attachment checks, and the blob it measures is reused for the write. (3) `MEMORY_LIVE_REFERENCE` is not a request refusal; it is reported by the hard-removal path. `GraphTxn::forget(id, delete = true)` (`crates/medulla-graph-core/src/graph/txn_maintenance.rs:184`), the one chokepoint reached by `evict_below` (:206) and `maintain` (:231), refuses to remove a node that has an inbound edge (`self.topo.graph.edges_directed(idx, Incoming)`) from a live node, and returns `false`; a live node is a node that exists and whose `forgotten` property is not `true`. The node stays with its edges. `evict_below` and `maintain` return the skipped ids as `live_referenced` beside `pruned`: `evict_below` returns `(pruned, live_referenced)` and `maintain` returns `(decayed, pruned, live_referenced)`; the result contracts `EvictBelow` (`crates/medulla-protocol-types/src/result_contract/graph.rs:60`, now `Raw<(Vec<String>, Vec<String>)>`) and `Maintain` (:122, now `Raw<(usize, Vec<String>, Vec<String>)>`) and the Python client in `medulla/generated` change in the same commit (no wrapper keeps the old shape). The gateway arms (`gateway_graph_routes.rs:581` and `:594`) return the lists. The mark path (`delete = false`) is unaffected, and a live node is never `forgotten` by consolidation. `RETENTION_LEGAL_HOLD` is owned by R617.4. A refusal changes no state. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R652.11` | **Proven standing rule `PROVEN_STANDING`.** Stage: 10 Learn, served by `Method::Claims`. Standing is a derived value, not a lifecycle: no field stores it and no event moves it. It is recomputed from the evidence on every read. Rule `PROVEN_STANDING`: a claim is `proven` when at least one of its evidence records holds a receipt with verdict `pass`, `has_sorry` false, and every axiom in `axioms` equal to an element of `PROOF_STANDARD_AXIOMS` (exact, case-sensitive comparison, because Lean names are case-sensitive). Otherwise the claim is `unproven`. A receipt with a `fail` verdict, with `has_sorry` true, or with any other axiom never grants standing, and it stays recorded and readable. The standard-axiom set is the constant `PROOF_STANDARD_AXIOMS`, not a knob: there is no `claims.proof_standard_axioms` knob, no `KnobValue::Text` and no change to `claim_knobs`; the set changes with a release, not with configuration. The `ProofReceipt` fixture in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/` that writes `quot.sound` is corrected to `Quot.sound` in the same change. Evidence on a retired claim is refused as today. Proven standing does not change `ClaimState`; `Advance` keeps its log-odds guard. A receipt records without refusal when it carries a non-standard axiom: standing stays `unproven`, and the axiom list is the answer of R652.13. Writes: none. Depends: R652.10. The rank is `confidence_ppm` times `recency_ppm` divided by 1000000, with `confidence_ppm` the logistic of the claim's log-odds and recency as 0.5 to the power of age over `knob participant.card_recency_half_life`. The function adds claims in rank order while the sum of `token_estimate` (one token per four characters of the statement) stays within the budget, and the first claim that does not fit ends the card. Knob `participant.card_recency_half_life` default 30 d, [1 d, 365 d], Tunable. The card ranks the claims of one subject and observer that state a sentence, are not retired and fall inside the observer's own sessions. `plan_card_refresh` in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/participant_card.rs` recomputes the card from the claim store and `refresh_card` in `crates/medulla-h-graph/src/graph_ops/participant_card.rs` answers the operations that store it as a node of type `ParticipantCard` and write the `memory.card.updated` event (R073.6), or nothing when the digest did not change. One caller exists: after the `Claims` handler commits a lifecycle transition of a claim that has a perspective, the router (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/memory_events.rs`) refreshes the card of that subject and observer once and commits the operations as one `BatchUpdate`; a card is created by the first such transition. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R702.4` | **Refusal.** Stage: 10 Learn, served by `Method::CorrectionRecord`. Codes in the `REFUSALS` table: `CORRECTION_ROLE_REQUIRED` refuses an actor without the verified role `corrector`; `RULE_CONTRADICTS_INVARIANT` refuses a candidate that contradicts a stored invariant, as checked by R129; `OUTCOME_SELF_REPORTED` refuses a correction whose corrector equals the producer of the corrected action, so a self-reported outcome never enters calibration (R016). The corrector is the verified principal and the producer is the `actor` of the action record that `target` names; the request carries neither, so a corrector cannot attribute a correction to another actor. `target` must name a visible `ActionRecord` node of the caller's tenant. An absent record, a hidden one, another tenant's and a node of another class all refuse `CORRECTION_NOT_FOUND` with one message, so the refusal is no existence oracle. A refusal commits no effect. `RULE_CONTRADICTS_INVARIANT` is the code R129.5 already registers, so the `correction` table holds `CORRECTION_ROLE_REQUIRED`, `OUTCOME_SELF_REPORTED` and `CORRECTION_NOT_FOUND` (R702.5) and reuses the R129 code. The role is read from `VerifiedRequestContext::roles()`. The candidate carries the `task_class` read from the corrected action record (`action_kind:<actionKind>`), and its rule id is the `sha256:` digest of its rule text (R702.2). It is checked as `GuardrailRule { rule_id: <candidate rule id>, applies_to_class: <task class>, source_generation: <receipt_id> }` against every invariant of `published_rule_invariants(tenant)` whose `on_class` is that task class, through `check_rule_against_invariants`; an invariant of another class does not govern it. The order is role, action record (`CORRECTION_NOT_FOUND`), self-report, shape (R702.1), invariant, then the embedding space. Depends: R702.3, R010.100.1. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R704.2` | **Behavior.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints. Add `Correlator` and `match_playbook` to `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/playbook.rs`. `Correlator` keeps one `VecDeque` of events per service and evicts events older than `knob playbook.window` default 300 `[10, 86400]` seconds. Insert is O(1) amortized. A service is flapping when it has at least `knob playbook.flap_min_events` default 3 `[2, 100]` state-change events in the window. `match_playbook` looks up the trigger kind in a hash map. A `Correlator` is built per request from the caller's own events and refuses an event older than the newest one held for its service with `CorrelateError::OutOfOrder`. Writes: none. Depends: R704.1, R179.2. Code `ER_CROSS_TENANT` refuses, in the candidate stage, a pair that joins a node the asking tenant holds (a visible embedded node of the graph `er.graph`) with one it does not hold; another tenant's node and an absent node answer alike, so nothing about the other tenant is revealed. Code `ER_BELOW_THRESHOLD` abstains (`AbstainReason::Family`) when the highest scored proposal is under the head's certified act threshold of R032.2. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R800.2` | **Behaviour: next parent, scoreboard and front digest.** Stage: 10 Learn, op `AnalyticsJob`. Code: add `ParetoFront::next_parent(seed)`, `ParetoFront::scoreboard()` and `ParetoFront::digest()` in `crates/medulla-program/src/optimize/front.rs`. Crowding distance uses every score and cost, each normalized by its front range. Boundary candidates get infinite distance. `next_parent` runs a binary tournament with SplitMix64 seeded by `seed`. The larger distance wins; ties pick the lower id. `scoreboard` ranks by `scores[0]` divided by `max(cost_micro_usd, 1)`, descending, ties by id. `digest` is SHA-256 over canonical JSON of candidates sorted by id, 64 lowercase hex characters. An earlier ABORT of the same txn id refuses with `CERTIFICATE_DECIDED_ABORT` and reserves nothing; an earlier COMMIT resumes (the owners hold their reservations and only the record write is left). Both owners reserve under the txn id `decision-commit:<record_id>:<idempotency_key>`; a refusal of either decides ABORT. The vote is the commit's stale-catalog check (`expected_catalog_digest` against the record's), taken before the decision: a NO decides ABORT and both owners resolve from it. A COMMIT decides durably before `store.commit_decision_record` runs. The check `participants.len() < 2` in `commit_cross_shard_inner` (`mod.rs:462`) counts owner participants with graph groups, so a transaction with one graph slice and one owner participant is admitted. A transaction with graph slices only keeps its current behaviour, and its ordinary decision row carries no certificate. An ABORT never expires. A COMMIT replay of a decided transaction returns the original outcome. A crash between the terminal write and either owner's resolve is finished by the same read on restart. Refusals: `CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED`, `CERTIFICATE_INTENT_CHANGED` (a replay of the same txn id with a different `request_digest`), `CERTIFICATE_LEGACY_ROW`, and `CERTIFICATE_DECIDED_ABORT`, all registered in the `REFUSALS` of `certificate.rs` and as `DecisionErrorCode` variants (the code first in the served error), plus `DECISION_COORDINATOR_UNAVAILABLE` when the engine has no durable redb backend (the handler refuses by name, with no local fallback). The item is a node whose row records `held_item_kind`, `content_digest` and `lifecycle` (`active` or `retired`); a program row also records `compiled_by`, `verified_by`, `verification_ref` and `verification_passes`; a proposal row records `critique_ref`, `critique_digest` and `critique_verdict` (`accept` or `reject`); the terms are declared in `orchestration-v1.ttl` (`:HeldItem`). Rule: an item absent from the caller's view or of another kind refuses `HELD_ITEM_UNKNOWN`; the stored digest must equal `content_digest`, else `DIGEST_MISMATCH`. A program needs a verification record whose verifier differs from its compiler, else `VERIFIER_NOT_INDEPENDENT`. Its pass count must reach decision-policy knob `held_item.min_passes` (default 2, [1, 20], count; `knob_families`, DE-R059.1-KNOBS), else `PASSES_INSUFFICIENT`. A retired program refuses `RETIRED`. An output proposal needs a critique record whose `critique_digest` equals its content digest, else `CRITIQUE_MISSING`; its verdict then answers `admitted` (`accept`) or `rejected` (`reject`). The refusals are family abstentions under their registered codes. The answer is the option `admitted` or `rejected`. Evidence: premise `verification:<ref>` (program) or `critique:<ref>` (proposal), class `Observation`, bound to the item. Writes: none. Depends: `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R001.101`, `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R179`.
