| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R651.12` | **Derive worker writes conclusions as claims.** Stage: 10 learn; operations `DeriveConclusions` (read) and `Participant` `CompleteDerivation` (write). The engine calls no model in process. The task of queue `memory.derive` (R651.11) is claimed by an external model worker over the jobs seam, and the worker proposes its conclusions back over the wire. The engine owns three things around that worker. (1) `select_turns` and `ParticipantReadOp::DeriveInput { payload_ref }` (the payload the queue task names): given the task's `DerivePayload`, it reads the turns of the payload range through the `GraphView` of the job principal. It narrows them by `resolve_scope_sessions` (R651.9). It keeps turns by the subject for `observer = System` or `observer = subject`. It keeps turns by other members for `observe_others`. It answers `DeriveInput { key, turns, max_conclusions }`, each turn `{ turn_id, speaker, text, timestamp_ms }` in stored order, and `max_conclusions` is `knob memory.derive_max_conclusions`. A job whose range starts after the stored `DeriveCheckpoint.last_turn_id` (a turn of the key sits between them that no job has derived) answers `DERIVE_ORDER_HELD` and the worker releases and retries the task. (2) The worker writes each conclusion with `ClaimOp::Propose` (perspective = the key's subject and observer) and `ClaimOp::RecordEvidence` of the `Claims` handler (R652.3). The evidence is the turn ids, with channel `mined`. A conclusion's claim id is `conclusion_claim_prefix(key)` (which `DeriveInput.claim_prefix` hands the worker) followed by the SHA-256 of the whitespace-normalised, case-folded text, and the evidence's `source_digest` is `turn:<turn id>`, so a conclusion that repeats an existing one proposes the same claim (propose is idempotent on the id) and only adds evidence; the cosine merge of `knob memory.merge_cosine` is the worker's own affair and the engine holds no second memory store. (3) `ParticipantOp::CompleteDerivation { payload_ref, claims_written }` is the one write the engine performs for a job. The claims live in the claim store, so the graph is the authority on the count: the decide arm of `Method::Participant` counts the claim records of the tenant whose id carries the key's prefix and whose evidence cites a turn of the payload range, refuses `claims_written` above `max_conclusions` (`DERIVE_CONCLUSION_LIMIT`) and any other count that differs from that number (`DERIVATION_COUNT_MISMATCH`), then continues to the graph write, which refuses a range that starts after a gap (`DERIVE_ORDER_HELD`), upserts the `DeriveCheckpoint` node of the key (`last_turn_id` = the payload's `last_turn_id`) and writes one `memory.derivation.completed` event node (R073.6) in the same batch. The worker then acks the task with `TaskQueueAck`. Completing an already completed range is a no-op. Knob `memory.derive_max_conclusions` default 8, [1, 32], claims, Tunable. Writes: the checkpoint and one outbox event; the claims and evidence are written by the worker through `Claims`. Depends: R651.11, R652.9, R652.3, R651.7, R073.6, R179.8. Shape: `select_turns`, `conclusion_claim_id`, `derive_held` and `advance_checkpoint` as pure functions in `crates/medulla-decision-stats/src/decision/participant_derive.rs` and `crates/medulla-h-graph/src/graph_ops/participant_derive.rs`; reuse the claim writer of `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/claims.rs`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R134.111` | **Bounded explicit task graphs (rollup).** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints. Add `knob width.latency_p95_cap_ms`, default 2000, range [100, 600000], ms, Tunable. Add `knob width.window_max_age_s`, default 600, range [30, 86400], s, Tunable. Set `width.error_hi` default to 0.02 and `width.error_lo` default to 0.005. The model and width pair is scored jointly. The score of a model is its tier distance from the target tier (the error rate and the latency set the target tier and width: error at or above `width.error_hi` moves up one tier and narrows, a p95 above the cap narrows and keeps the model, error at or below `width.error_lo` widens). On an equal score the lower predicted cost (mean per-run cost in micro-units x width x the option's optional `cost_weight`, default 1) wins, then the lower model IRI. An unknown latency abstains `LATENCY_UNKNOWN`; too few runs (an unknown error rate) abstains `INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLES`. A request with `mid_run` true cannot widen and refuses `WIDEN_MID_RUN`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R818` | **Probe selection from a goal.** Stage: 2 Candidates to 7 Conclude, served by `Decide` with new `QuestionKind::ProbeSelection` (family `probe_selection`). The request holds `goal_text` (param `goal_text`, text, required) and optional target categories (param `target_categories`, `TypedValue::IriList`). Candidates are `CandidateSource::AgentLibrary` over the tenant's `RedTeamAttack` and `RedTeamTransform` components (R138.1). | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R825` | **Model capacity question.** Parent `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R112`. Add `QuestionKind::ModelCapacity`. The handler `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_model_capacity.rs` runs the controllers of `crates/medulla-resource/src/admission.rs`. These are `ModelCapacityController`, `CircuitBreaker` and `CognitiveScheduler`. They run over the recorded latency and outcome observations of one model endpoint, which the caller sends in the request; the handler reads no usage ledger and no decision log. Request parameters (typed `TypedValue::Text` holding JSON, read with `json_param`, `int_param` and `text_param` of `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/support.rs`): `capacity_observations` is a `Vec<CapacityObservation { at_ms: u64, latency_ms: u64, outcome: CapacityOutcome }>` with `CapacityOutcome` closed `success` or `failure`, at most 1,000 entries, `at_ms` non-decreasing (else `PARAMETER_INVALID`, the existing code); `capacity_bounds` is `CapacityBounds { group: String, initial: u32, min: u32, ceiling: u32, cell_ceiling: u32, group_slots: u32, now_ms: u64 }` with `now_ms` at or after the last `at_ms`. All types are new, `deny_unknown_fields`, in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/model_capacity.rs` declared in `decision.rs`. The one declared option is `capacity`, checked by `single_option`. Rule: build `ModelCapacityController::new(initial, min, ceiling, cell_ceiling, knob capacity.latency_target_ms)` and `CircuitBreaker::new(knob capacity.breaker_failures, knob capacity.breaker_cooldown_ms)`. For each observation in order call `on_latency(latency_ms)`, `breaker.tick(at_ms)` and `breaker.observe(Some(outcome), at_ms)`; then `breaker.tick(now_ms)`. Build `CognitiveScheduler::new(InferenceBudget { tokens_per_window: group_slots })` and call `request` with one one-token `Normal` process (id `<group>:<n>`) up to `effective_limit(&breaker)` times, stopping at the first answer that is not `Admit`; no other limiter exists in the handler. The answer is one option `capacity:<json of CapacityAnswer>` with `CapacityAnswer { limit: u32 (controller.limit()), effective_limit: u32, breaker: BreakerKind, granted: u32 (the count of `CognitiveDecision::Admit` answers; the scheduler's own `used` is private), group_slots_free: u32 (group_slots - granted) }` and `BreakerKind` closed `closed`, `half_open`, `open`. A `ceiling` above `cell_ceiling` makes `ModelCapacityController::new` return `CONCURRENCY_ABOVE_CELL_CEILING`; the handler turns that into the abstention `AbstainReason::PolicyLoosening { field: "ceiling" }`, built as `abstained` of `support.rs` builds `Abstained`. Evidence: one `Claim` premise `capacity:observations=<n>@<sha256 hex of the parameter text>` (the observations are the caller's claims).  Knobs: `knob capacity.latency_target_ms` 2,000 [50, 60,000] ms, `knob capacity.breaker_failures` 5 [1, 100], `knob capacity.breaker_cooldown_ms` 30,000 [1,000, 600,000] ms. A limit never exceeds the declared cell ceiling; a request above it abstains `PolicyLoosening`. Writes nothing. Depends: `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R001.101`. Shape: new `ModelCapacity` variant in `QuestionKind` (`statistical.rs:58`); the handler only feeds recorded observations to the three existing controllers and does not copy their logic; `PolicyLoosening` is the existing abstain reason. | Test: `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/model_capacity_tests.rs::limit_narrows_on_latency_and_never_exceeds_ceiling` (L3) sends 10 observations over the target and asserts a halved `limit`, then 3 under it and asserts a `limit` that grows by one each and stays at or below `ceiling`; sends `breaker_failures` consecutive failures and asserts `breaker` `open` with `effective_limit` 0 and `granted` 0; sends `now_ms` after the cooldown and asserts `half_open` with `effective_limit` 1; sends `ceiling` above `cell_ceiling` and asserts the `PolicyLoosening` abstention; sends a decreasing `at_ms` and asserts `PARAMETER_INVALID`. |

This row owns the decision side only: the family, its refusal codes and knobs, and the seam the merge handler calls. The call from `merge_conflicts` and the write of the resolution belong to `MEDULLA-BRANCH-MERGE-R005`, which consumes this row; a handler crate never calls a sibling handler crate, so the graph side reaches the decision only through the seam. **Request body.** `TypedValue::ResolveConflict(Box<ConflictCandidates>)` (`statistical.rs:482`); `ConflictCandidates { entity: String, candidate_a: ConflictCandidate, candidate_b: ConflictCandidate }` in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/statistical/declared.rs:164`, `deny_unknown_fields`. `ConflictCandidate` holds `source_reliability: f64` and `confidence: f64` (each in [0, 1]), `valid_from: u64`, `valid_until: Option<u64>`, `tx_from: u64` (milliseconds) and `evidence_refs: Vec<String>`; equality compares the two floats bitwise. **Rule.** score = `ConflictCandidate::score()` = reliability x confidence, `f64`, checked finite before comparison. The higher score wins when the gap is at least knob `conflict.min_margin` (`KnobValue::DecimalMicros`, default 150000, range [0, 1000000], unit ratio). A smaller gap breaks the tie by the later `valid_from` only when `ConflictCandidate::overlaps` holds and knob `conflict.recency_tiebreak` is 1 (`KnobValue::Integer`, default 0, range [0, 1], unit flag). Both knobs are `KNOBS` of `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/resolve_conflict.rs`, read through `DecisionPolicy::knob`. **Refusals.** `CONFLICT_UNRESOLVED` (gap below the margin, no tie-break), `CONFLICT_POLICY_MISSING` (the request policy is `DecisionPolicyRef::Default`, no pin), `CONFLICT_NONFINITE` (a score is NaN or infinite): the `REFUSALS` of `resolve_conflict.rs`, joined to `codes::FAMILY_TABLES` under `QuestionKind::ResolveConflict` (`crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/codes.rs:615`). Premises: `conflict:score_a=<value>`, `conflict:score_b=<value>`, `knob:conflict.min_margin=<value>`. The answer names `candidate_a` or `candidate_b`. The implementation is `ConflictDeciderSeam` in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:80`: it refuses a question whose kind is not `ResolveConflict` with `PARAMETER_INVALID` and otherwise returns the first record of `serve`. `crates/medulla-server/src/seams_install.rs:47` installs it on the `conflict` slot of `SeamRegistry` (`crates/medulla-server-api/src/api/registry.rs:35`) at startup. MEDULLA-BRANCH-MERGE-R005 builds one `DecideRequest` per `ConflictRecord` with a pinned policy, the verified tenant as `tenant_id` and the param above, then calls `decide_conflict`; an abstention leaves the conflict open. Depends: MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R001.101, MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R179.1, MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R010.100.1. Caller chain: `Method::Decide` (`crates/medulla-server-router/src/dispatch/router/decision_plane.rs:112`) -> `handle_decide` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs:60`) -> `serve` (`stat_decide.rs:109`) -> `decide_blocking` (`stat_decide.rs:401`) -> `execute` (`crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_executor.rs`) -> `family::for_kind` (R001.101) -> `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/resolve_conflict.rs`; seam path: `merge_conflicts` (MEDULLA-BRANCH-MERGE-R005) -> `medulla_server_api::api::conflict_decider::decide_conflict` -> `ConflictDeciderSeam::decide_conflict` -> `serve`. Shape: family file `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/family/resolve_conflict.rs`; types `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/resolve_conflict.rs` and `statistical/declared.rs`; seam `crates/medulla-server-api/src/api/conflict_decider.rs`; no second decider and no direct call between handler crates. | Test: `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/resolve_conflict_tests.rs::winner_by_margin_tie_and_abstain_codes` (L3) asserts the winner by margin, the recency tie-break, each refusal code and its premises, that `ConflictDeciderSeam::decide_conflict` answers the same winner as `Decide`, and a cross-tenant request refused with `ACCESS_DENIED`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R829.2` | **Option features for capability ranking are computed by medulla from candidate text.** Stage: 4 Features. For the four entries of R829.1 medulla computes, per candidate, the versioned feature set of R021: `name_overlap` (query terms found in the candidate name after stopword removal and plural folding), `description_overlap`, `term_rarity_weighted_overlap` (each query term weighted by `ln(1 + (N + 1) / (df + 1))` over the call's candidates, name matches counted twice), `name_coverage` (share of the name's terms matched, the tie-break) and `semantic_similarity` (cosine of the query and candidate-text embeddings when the embedding model is ready, else absent). These are exactly the quantities that arbora's deleted scorers computed, now owned here; a candidate with no term match scores zero. The pinned head ranks by the calibrated probability, and `rank.item_score` (R130) is `term_rarity_weighted_overlap`. Knobs (registered, never constants): new `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/capability_rank.rs` declares `pub const KNOBS: &[KnobSpec]` with `decision.rank.name_weight` (unit `weight`, `KnobValue::DecimalMicros` default 2_000_000, min 0, max 16_000_000, `KnobSafety::Tunable`) and `decision.rank.semantic_weight` (same unit, default 1_000_000, min 0, max 16_000_000, `Tunable`), plus `pub fn name_weight(policy: &DecisionPolicy) -> f64` and `pub fn semantic_weight(policy: &DecisionPolicy) -> f64` (micros divided by 1,000,000, as `resolve_conflict::min_margin` does). The module is declared in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision.rs`, its `KNOBS` joins the list in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/knob_families.rs` (beside `super::resolve_conflict::KNOBS`) and is appended to the `QuestionKind::Rank` arm of the knob table in `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_decide.rs` (:893-925). Without the `query` feature the closure is `None`. Caller chain: `family/rank.rs` -> `candidates.rs` rank arm -> `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/features/capability_text.rs::capability_features`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R134.111.19` | **Foreach step model and static checks.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints. A tool step may carry `foreach: TaskPlanForeach { source: ForeachSource, max_items: u32 }` beside `call`, declared after `assignee` in `TaskPlanTask`. `ForeachSource` is `{"$ref": "steps.<task_id>.output[.<json.path>]"}` and names a JSON array; the engine writes it in the one canonical reference form. `max_items` is an integer from 1 to 256. Inside the call arguments, `{"$ref": "item.<json.path>"}` names the current item and `{"$ref": "item_index"}` names its zero-based index. The source follows the binding rules of R134.111.9, including the direct `depends_on` check. A plan may hold at most 8 foreach steps. One foreach step expands to at most 256 calls, and a plan expands to at most 1,024, counting `max_items` for a foreach step and one for every other tool step. An item reference is not a binding: it adds no edge, and the call keeps it in its canonical form (`item.<path>` follows the path grammar and bounds of R134.111.9). The plan digest covers `foreach` through the canonical task body; the policy digest and revision are unchanged, so a plan without foreach digests as before. ### Semantic program reuse (R135.16, R135.17)

| ID | Requirement | Verification |

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R135.16` | **Semantic program lookup by request text (rollup).** Stage: 10 Learn for indexing at commit, then 2 Candidates and 3 Policy and constraints for lookup. Served operations `DecisionLog` (`DecisionLogOp::RunRecord` with `RunRecord::CompiledProgram`) and `Decide` with `QuestionKind::ProgramLookup`. A commit may carry example phrasings and a match threshold. The engine embeds the task signature and each phrasing through the bounded embedding provider of MEDULLA-FEDERATED-QUERY-R040.5.4. It stores the vectors in the semantic index of the program's graph. A lookup that names `request_text` receives one bound program match or an abstention. An exact signature answers first, with no embedding call. Otherwise the engine embeds the request text once and probes the program vectors. It returns the nearest program when the cosine reaches that program's threshold. Every parameter must bind from the request text or from a declared fixed value. No generative model runs on this path. Children `.1` to `.6` are model, behavior, wiring, refusal, evidence and hot-path proof. Writes: `DecisionLog` only. Depends: R135.3, R135.4, R135.5, MEDULLA-FEDERATED-QUERY-R040.5.4. | Test: `crates/medulla-h-decide/src/decide/stat_tests/program_match_tests.rs::request_text_finds_the_nearest_program_and_binds_it` (new) (L3) commits a program with two phrasings. It looks the program up by one phrasing's text under another task signature. It asserts the match, the bindings, the bound steps and the R135.16.5 premises. A request below the threshold abstains with `PROGRAM_BELOW_THRESHOLD`. |
Depends: MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R135.3, MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R135.4, MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R135.5, MEDULLA-FEDERATED-QUERY-R040.5.4

| `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R135.16.2` | **Behavior: index build, slot binding and nearest-program selection.** Stage: 10 Learn (index build) and 3 Policy and constraints (binding and selection). Pure functions with no I/O in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/program_store/semantic.rs`. `build_match_index(trace: &RunTraceRecord, program: &CompiledProgram, phrasings: &[ProgramPhrasing], threshold_micros: Option<i64>) -> Result<ProgramMatchIndex, ProgramError>`. Rule 1: a threshold must lie in [500000, 1000000]. Rule 2: each phrasing is trimmed and holds 1 to 512 bytes. A placeholder is `{p<k>}` and must name a declared program parameter. Two placeholders need literal text between them. Every phrasing names the same placeholder set. Rule 3: `slots` is the sorted placeholder set. `slot_kinds: BoundedVec<ProgramParameterKind, 64>` (serde default) holds the kind (`text`, `int` or `bool`) of each slot in `slots` order, taken from the parameter kind of the same first-occurrence walk (`text` when the walk has none), and `slot_kinds[i]` is the kind Rule 7 converts the capture of `slots[i]` by. `fixed` holds every other parameter with the literal it took at its first occurrence in the trace. The walk is the first-occurrence walk of `compile_program`. With no phrasings, `slots` and `fixed` are empty. Rule 4: the index holds one `StepTemplate` per trace step, in order. A `tool_call` step splits `action_ref` at its first `/` into a non-empty `server` and a non-empty `tool`. Each argument maps its name to the parameter that `compile_program` gave its literal. A `model_call` step keeps empty `server`, `tool` and `arguments`. `executable` is true when one or more steps are `tool_call`, every `tool_call` reference splits, and no step is `other`. `bind_request(index: &ProgramMatchIndex, request_text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Binding>, Unbound>`. Rule 5: whether a program has parameters is read from the step templates (an argument of any `StepTemplate` names a parameter), because an index with no phrasings holds neither `slots` nor `fixed`. A program with no parameters binds to an empty list. A program with parameters and no phrasings is unbound. The order of the returned bindings is the `slot` bindings in `slots` order, then the `fixed` bindings in `fixed` order. Rule 6: trim the request text and collapse each whitespace run to one space. Normalize each literal segment of a phrasing the same way. Compare literal segments with ASCII case folding. Try the phrasings in stored order. A placeholder captures the shortest non-empty text before the next literal segment. A trailing placeholder captures the rest of the text. A phrasing fits only when its segments cover the whole text. A placeholder that occurs twice in one phrasing must capture equal text. Rule 7: trim each capture. Kind `int` parses a decimal `i64`. Kind `bool` accepts `true` or `false` with ASCII case folding. Kind `text` keeps the capture. The first fitting phrasing whose captures all convert binds the slots with source `slot`. The fixed values bind the remaining parameters with source `fixed`. No fit returns `Unbound { parameters }` with the slot names. `select_match(candidates: &ProgramCandidates, threshold_of: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<Option<i64>>, default_micros: i64) -> Selection`, with `Selection` closed: `Selected { task_signature: String, node_id: String, score_micros: i64, threshold_micros: i64 }`, `BelowThreshold { score_micros: i64, threshold_micros: i64 }` and `NoProgram`; `node_id` is the node of the program's best hit. Rule 8: a program's score is the highest score of its hits. Order programs by score, highest first, then by task signature in byte order. The first program whose index exists is the candidate. Its threshold is its own `threshold_micros`, else `default_micros`. A score below the threshold returns `BelowThreshold { score_micros, threshold_micros }`. No candidate returns `NoProgram`. `bind_steps(index, bindings) -> Vec<BoundStep>` keeps the `tool_call` templates in order. Each argument takes the bound value of its parameter. Refusals: R135.16.4. Writes: none. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R135.16.4` | **Refusal: phrasings, thresholds and matches.** Stage: 3 Policy and constraints. Served operations `DecisionLog` and `Decide`. Code: the codes are declared in `crates/medulla-decision-types/src/decision/program_store/semantic.rs` and joined to `program_store::REFUSALS`. Commit refusals return `StatisticalErrorCode::ParameterInvalid` with the code leading the detail. They store no row and write no graph method. `PHRASING_INVALID`: more than 16 phrasings, or a phrasing that is empty or longer than 512 bytes. `PHRASING_SLOT_UNKNOWN`: a placeholder names no declared parameter. `PHRASING_SLOTS_ADJACENT`: two placeholders have no literal text between them. `PHRASING_SLOTS_DIFFER`: two phrasings name different placeholder sets. `MATCH_THRESHOLD_OUT_OF_RANGE`: a threshold outside [500000, 1000000]. `PROGRAM_EMBEDDING_SPACE_MISMATCH`: the graph declares a space other than the configured space. A provider failure refuses with its own code: `EMBED_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `EMBED_VECTOR_INVALID` or `EMBED_PROVIDER_FAILED`. Lookup refusals return `PARAMETER_INVALID`. `REQUEST_TEXT_TOO_LONG`: `request_text` longer than 4096 bytes. `PROGRAM_GRAPH_REQUIRED`: `request_text` without `program_graph`. `PROGRAM_CANDIDATES_RESERVED`: the caller supplied `program_candidates`. Lookup abstentions are `AbstainReason::Family`, so the caller plans normally. `NO_PROGRAM`: no exact program and no hit. `PROGRAM_BELOW_THRESHOLD`: the best score is below the threshold. The detail names both values. `PROGRAM_SLOTS_UNBOUND`: no phrasing fits, or a capture does not convert. The detail names the unbound parameters. `PROGRAM_NOT_EXECUTABLE`: the index has `executable` false. `PROGRAM_EMBEDDING_UNAVAILABLE`: the candidates carry `unavailable`. The detail names the cause. A graph or a node that the caller may not see behaves as absent. Writes: none. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R869.1` | **ActionRecord model.** Subsystem: decisions and provenance. Ontology: add to `crates/medulla-core/ontology/action-v1.ttl` (prefix `:` is the file's existing `https://knuckles-team.github.io/ontology/core#`): class `:ActionRecord rdfs:subClassOf :ActionInvocation`; class `:FactUse rdfs:subClassOf :DomainEntity` (one fact read by one action); class `:RuleUse rdfs:subClassOf :DomainEntity` (one rule applied by one action). Properties: `:actionKind` (datatype, domain `:ActionRecord`, `xsd:string`, closed values `tool_call`, `approval`, `filing`, `money_movement`, `publish`); `:actor` (object, domain `:ActionRecord`, the acting principal's node); `:usedFact` (object, `:ActionRecord` to `:FactUse`); `:factNode` (datatype `xsd:string`, the node id of the fact; a string, not an edge, so a traversal never reaches the fact's current image); `:factRevision` (`xsd:integer` ≥ 0, the graph version the action read the node at, the version `GraphCore::node_properties_at` answers); `:factDigest` (`xsd:string`, `sha256:` plus 64 lowercase hex of SHA-256 over the node's msgpack property blob at that version, the exact bytes `node_properties_at` returns); `:usedRule` (object, `:ActionRecord` to `:RuleUse`); `:ruleNode` (`xsd:string`), `:ruleVersion` (`xsd:integer`) and `:ruleDigest` (`xsd:string`, `sha256:` plus 64 hex); `:approvedBy` (object, `:ActionRecord` to `:GateDecision` of `business_ops-v1.ttl`); `:causedBy` (object, `:ActionRecord` to an earlier `:ActionRecord`); `:actionOutcome` (`xsd:string`, the caller's outcome text); `:noInputs` (`xsd:string`, the stated reason a record used no fact). The existing `:idempotencyKey` of `orchestration-v1.ttl` is reused with domain unchanged, not redeclared. Shapes: new `crates/medulla-core/ontology/action-v1.shapes.ttl`, wired into the `action` `CoreSpec` of `crates/medulla-graph-core/src/graph/schema_sources.rs` (today `shapes: None`) as `shapes: Some(include_str!("../../../medulla-core/ontology/action-v1.shapes.ttl"))`, the `business_ops` pattern. `:ActionRecordShape` (`sh:targetClass :ActionRecord`): `:actionKind` exactly one, `sh:in` the five values; `:actor` exactly one; `:idempotencyKey` exactly one; `sh:or ( [ sh:path :usedFact ; sh:minCount 1 ] [ sh:path :noInputs ; sh:minCount 1 ] )`. `:FactUseShape`: `:factNode` exactly one; `:factRevision` exactly one, `xsd:integer`, `sh:minInclusive 0`; `:factDigest` exactly one, `sh:pattern "^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$"`. `:RuleUseShape`: the same for `:ruleNode`, `:ruleVersion` and `:ruleDigest`. A record is append-only: no writer updates an `:ActionRecord` node; a correction is a new record whose `:causedBy` names the corrected one. Caller chain: the shapes are read by the graph schema at open through `GraphSchemaSources`; records are written by R869.2. Shape: two ontology files and one `CoreSpec` field. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R869.2` | **Write path and refusals.** Wire: `SourceBatchKind::ActionRecords` and `SourceBatchExtension::ActionRecords(BoundedVec<SourceJson, MAX_ACTION_RECORDS>)` with `pub const MAX_ACTION_RECORDS: usize = 256` in `crates/medulla-source-types/src/source_ingestion/batch_kind.rs` (and the arm in `SourceBatchExtension::kind`). New `crates/medulla-source-types/src/source_action_record.rs` holds the typed item `ActionRecordItem { idempotency_key: String, action_kind: ActionKind, actor: String, used_facts: BoundedVec<FactUseItem, 64>, used_rules: BoundedVec<RuleUseItem, 16>, approved_by: Option<String>, caused_by: Option<String>, outcome: Option<String>, no_inputs: Option<String> }`, `FactUseItem { node_id: String, revision: u64, content_digest: String }`, `RuleUseItem { rule_id: String, version: u64, digest: String }` and the `Copy` enum `ActionKind { ToolCall, Approval, Filing, MoneyMovement, Publish }` (serde `snake_case`), all `deny_unknown_fields`; the Python mirror goes into `medulla/generated/models.py`. Validator: new `crates/medulla-h-ingest/src/source_ingestion/action_record.rs`, declared `pub mod action_record;` in `source_ingestion.rs` under `#[cfg(all(feature = "redb", feature = "blob"))]` like `transcript`, and called from one new `Some(SourceBatchExtension::ActionRecords(items))` arm of the extension match in `prepare`, beside the `Transcripts` arm. Functions: `decode_action_items(items: &[SourceJson]) -> Result<Vec<ActionRecordItem>, String>`; `action_node_id(tenant: &str, key: &str) -> Result<String, String>` = `"action:"` plus `Digest256::framed(b"eg/action-record/v1", &[tenant.as_bytes(), key.as_bytes()])?.to_hex()`; `item_digest(item) -> Digest256` = SHA-256 over `serde_json::to_vec(item)` (struct field order), stored as property `content_digest` in the form `sha256:<64 hex>`; `admit_actions(tenant, items, reads: &ActionReads) -> Result<ActionAdmission, String>`, where `ActionReads` holds the held action nodes, the held gate-decision and approval-request nodes (read with `persistence.read_node`, as `read_held_containers` does) and the graph's `GraphCore` (`ServerState.registry.get(ctx.graph_name)`), whose edges `admit_actions` reads for `decisionRequest`. Checks, per item in batch order, all before any write: (1) `ACTION_RECORD_INVALID` for an empty key or actor, a record with no fact and no `no_inputs`, a digest not of the `sha256:` plus 64 lowercase hex form, or a `caused_by` that names no held `ActionRecord`; (2) a held node at `action_node_id` with the same `content_digest` is an idempotent repeat: no method is emitted and the receipt names the held node id; a held node with another digest refuses `ACTION_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`; (3) for each used fact, `GraphCore::node_properties_at(node_id, revision)` must answer `Ok(Some(blob))` with `sha256:` plus hex SHA-256 of `blob` equal to `content_digest`; `Ok(None)`, `Err(NodeHistoryError::Future)`, `Err(NodeHistoryError::Retired)` or a different digest refuse `ACTION_FACT_REVISION_UNKNOWN` naming the node and revision; (4) for kind `money_movement`, `filing` or `publish`, `approved_by` must name a held node of type `GateDecision` with `gateOutcome = "approve"`, which has an outgoing edge `decisionRequest` to a held `ApprovalRequest` node (an edge read from the graph, never a string property naming a node: the graph is the authority) with `requestStatus` equal to `ApprovalStatus::Approved.stored()` (`"approved"`, `crates/medulla-core/src/approval_machine.rs`) and `requestActionKind` equal to the item's kind; otherwise `ACTION_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`. A refusal refuses the whole batch and writes nothing. The receipt node of the batch gains the property `action_records`, a JSON array of each item's `ActionRecord` node id in batch order (an idempotent repeat names the held node id). Methods for an admitted item: one node `action:<hex>` of type `ActionRecord` with `actionKind`, `actor`, `idempotencyKey`, `actionOutcome`, `noInputs`, `content_digest` and `tenant_id`; one node `action:<hex>:fact:<n>` of type `FactUse` per fact (n is its index) and `action:<hex>:rule:<n>` of type `RuleUse` per rule; edges `usedFact`, `usedRule`, `approvedBy` and `causedBy`; they commit through the existing ChangeEnvelope authority with the batch, and each node gets the batch's permission policy. Codes: four `ServerErrorCode` variants `ActionRecordInvalid`, `ActionIdempotencyConflict`, `ActionFactRevisionUnknown` and `ActionApprovalRequired` (`ACTION_RECORD_INVALID`, `ACTION_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`, `ACTION_FACT_REVISION_UNKNOWN`, `ACTION_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`) in `crates/medulla-types/src/contract/server_error_code.rs` beside `TranscriptInvalid`, each listed in `crates/medulla-capabilities/src/error_routing.rs` beside `TRANSCRIPT_INVALID`; errors are `<CODE>: <detail>`. Caller chain: `Method::SourceIngest` → `crates/medulla-h-ingest/src/source_ingestion.rs::prepare` → `action_record::admit_actions` → ChangeEnvelope commit. Shape: one types file, one validator file, one extension arm, four codes. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R869.3` | **The why chain.** The question "why did this action happen" is one UQL read, not an operation: `MATCH (:ActionRecord) WHERE idempotencyKey = $key |> TRAVERSE -[*]->{1,8} WITH PROOF`. From the record it follows `usedFact`, `usedRule`, `approvedBy` and `causedBy` (and the same edges of each earlier record) up to 8 hops, a fixed bound in the text; it adds no knob. Each fact appears as its `FactUse` row with `factNode`, `factRevision` and `factDigest`: the revision and digest the action used. The fact's current node is never reached, because `factNode` is a string property, not an edge (R869.1), so a later change to the fact does not change the answer. `WITH PROOF` attaches the per-row proof of `MEDULLA-FEDERATED-QUERY-R006`. The read runs through `handle_uql` under the caller's read scope, so rows the caller may not read are absent. The text is published once per tenant as the stored query `why_action` with one `Text` parameter `key` through `StoredQueryPut` (`crates/medulla-h-query/src/query/stored_query.rs`) and called as `CALL STORED why_action(key = '<key>')` (the UQL form binds a typed literal by name) or as `Method::StoredQueryCall`; the engine seeds nothing. The text parses as written: `-[*]->` is the any-relation outgoing edge pattern, `{1,8}` the hop range and `WITH PROOF` the statement annotation (`crates/medulla-uql/src/parser/traverse.rs`, `program.rs`). A UQL row carries the node id; the `FactUse`, `RuleUse` and gate rows are read by id for their `factRevision`, `factDigest` and `ruleDigest` properties. Writes: none. Caller chain: `Method::Uql` → `handle_uql` (`crates/medulla-h-query/src/query/uql_statement.rs`) → TRAVERSE over the four edges. Shape: no production file; one stored query published by the test and by consumers. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R713.5` | **Quality score and rank.** Stage: 6 Statistical rank, op `Rank`. A score passes by its `passed` flag, else when its value sits at or above the middle of its range. `quality_ppm = eval_pass_rate_ppm * eval_runs / (eval_runs + knob skill.quality.prior_runs)`. Knob `skill.quality.prior_runs` is Integer, default 20, bounds [1, 1000], unit runs. Rank orders by `quality_ppm` descending, then `eval_runs` descending, then `invocations` descending, then `skill_ref`. | `MEDULLA-DECISION-ENGINE-R713.8` | **Hot-path proof.** One L3 journey ingests 1,000 invocations from 30 pseudonyms with a mix of agent and user choice. It reads twelve measures and compares them with the golden vector. It ranks three skills and lists traces that failed their eval. It asks peers as a caller whose computed cohort holds 4 principals and sees `PEER_COHORT_TOO_SMALL`. Bench group `decide/skill_telemetry` (R178.1, `benches/skill_telemetry.rs`): ingest 1,000,000 invocations and read measures for one skill, p95 at most 50 ms. **Read index.** The reads do not scan a snapshot of the graph. The ingest batch stores three index keys on every `SkillInvocation` row: `skill_ref`, `principal_pseudonym` and `started_day` (the day bucket of `started_ms`, `started_ms / 86,400,000`, declared in the orchestration ontology and allowed by its shape). The handler reads through the graph's own property index over those keys (`GraphCore::nodes_by_property`, incrementally maintained by every write), intersects the lookups it needs (a window of at most 62 days adds its day buckets), decodes only those rows, and admits a row the way a filtered view does (`row_visibility` against the caller's isolation layer). Ingest checks a repeated id, the skill revision and the run trace through the same lookups (`run_id` for the trace), so a batch costs the batch and not the graph. Only `TracesByEval`, which follows score edges, takes a filtered snapshot. A row stored without `started_day` is outside a windowed read. Depends: R713.3, R713.4, R713.5, R713.6, R713.7.
